countries.name: Zimbabwe
countries.tagline: Where the smoke thunders, granite balances, and the Zambezi writes in light.

countries.name: Botswana
countries.tagline: Where the Kalahari drinks the Okavango and salt pans hold the sky.

countries.name: South Africa
countries.tagline: Two oceans, fynbos and the Drakensberg, the Cradle of Humankind and some of the oldest rocks on Earth.

countries.name: Namibia
countries.tagline: Red dunes, fog-fed life and ancient rock art where the desert meets the Atlantic.

countries.name: Malawi
countries.tagline: The Warm Heart of Africa: a lake of a thousand cichlids beneath sacred granite.

countries.name: Zambia
countries.tagline: Rivers, waterfalls and miombo, where ten million bats arrive with the rains.

countries.name: Mozambique
countries.tagline: Some 2,500 km of Indian Ocean coast: coral islands, dugong bays and sky-island forests.

countries.name: Algeria
countries.tagline: Africa’s largest country: Roman cities in the Tell, painted cliffs in the Tassili, volcanic peaks in the Hoggar.

countries.name: Egypt
countries.tagline: A green ribbon of Nile through the desert: pyramids, temples and whale bones in the sand.

countries.name: Libya
countries.tagline: Sand seas, crater lakes and Roman theatres facing the Mediterranean.

countries.name: Morocco
countries.tagline: From the High Atlas to the Saharan ergs: imperial medinas, red-earth kasbahs and argan forests.

countries.name: Sudan
countries.tagline: More pyramids than Egypt, along the Nile where the Blue and White rivers meet.

countries.name: Tunisia
countries.tagline: Carthage, Roman amphitheatres and blue-and-white villages above the Gulf of Tunis.

countries.name: Western Sahara
countries.tagline: A disputed Atlantic desert where the Sahara runs into the ocean.

countries.name: Benin
countries.tagline: Royal palaces of Dahomey, a town on stilts and the lions of Pendjari.

countries.name: Burkina Faso
countries.tagline: Painted royal courts, ancient iron furnaces and the sandstone needles of Sindou.

countries.name: Cabo Verde
countries.tagline: Volcano islands in the Atlantic, where morna music began and turtles return to nest.

countries.name: Côte d'Ivoire
countries.tagline: Rainforest of nut-cracking chimpanzees, lagoon towns and earthen Sudanese mosques.

countries.name: The Gambia
countries.tagline: A river nation of mangroves, stone circles and the island of Kunta Kinteh.

countries.name: Ghana
countries.tagline: Castles of the Gold Coast, Asante shrines and a canopy walk above the forest.

countries.name: Guinea
countries.tagline: The water tower of West Africa: the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers rise in its highlands.

countries.name: Guinea-Bissau
countries.tagline: Mangrove creeks and the Bijagós islands, where hippos swim in the sea.

countries.name: Liberia
countries.tagline: Upper Guinean rainforest, home of the pygmy hippo.

countries.name: Mali
countries.tagline: Mud-brick mosques of Djenné and Timbuktu, Dogon cliffs and the inland delta of the Niger.

countries.name: Mauritania
countries.tagline: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic: the Eye of Africa, desert libraries and a coast of birds.

countries.name: Niger
countries.tagline: The Aïr and the Ténéré, the minaret of Agadez and West Africa’s last giraffes.

countries.name: Nigeria
countries.tagline: Sacred groves, granite domes and mountain forests holding the rarest gorilla.

countries.name: Senegal
countries.tagline: Baobab country: a pink lake, the island of Gorée and pelicans by the hundred thousand.

countries.name: Sierra Leone
countries.tagline: Lion Mountains above Freetown, and rainforest islands rich in monkeys.

countries.name: Togo
countries.tagline: The tower-houses of the Batammariba, and forest waterfalls in the hills of Kpalimé.

countries.name: Angola
countries.tagline: The thundering Kalandula, the Namib’s northern edge and the giant sable of the miombo.

countries.name: Cameroon
countries.tagline: “Africa in miniature”: a volcano by the sea, rainforest, savanna and the Mandara highlands.

countries.name: Central African Republic
countries.tagline: Forest clearings where elephants gather by the hundred, at the heart of the continent.

countries.name: Chad
countries.tagline: Lakes in the Sahara, the arches of the Ennedi and the elephants of Zakouma.

countries.name: DR Congo
countries.tagline: The Congo basin: rainforest, lava lakes, okapi and the bonobo.

countries.name: Republic of the Congo
countries.tagline: Forest clearings of gorillas and elephants, and the Congo rapids at Brazzaville.

countries.name: Equatorial Guinea
countries.tagline: Volcanic Bioko, the rainforest of Río Muni and turtle beaches facing the Gulf of Guinea.

countries.name: Gabon
countries.tagline: Nearly 90% forest: surfing hippos, beach elephants and the mandrill’s painted face.

countries.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
countries.tagline: Two volcanic islands on the equator: cloud forest, a needle of rock and old cocoa plantations.

wonders.name: Victoria Falls
wonders.summary: The Zambezi drops into a narrow basalt chasm along a 1.7 km front on the Zimbabwe–Zambia border, throwing spray that can be seen from tens of kilometres away.
wonders.uniqueness: Often called the largest single sheet of falling water on Earth, combining its 1,708 m width with a drop of about 108 m. A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1989; its spray feeds a rainforest that grows on the cliff edge in a dry savanna.

wonders.name: Batoka Gorge
wonders.summary: Below Victoria Falls the Zambezi zig-zags through a chain of sheer basalt gorges, carved as the falls retreated upstream over thousands of years.
wonders.uniqueness: Each zig-zag records a former position of the waterfall, so the gorge works like a timeline written in rock. Its rapids rank among the world's great whitewater runs.

media.note: Stand-in: flight over the falls and the first gorges

wonders.name: Mana Pools
wonders.local_name: Mana — “four” in Shona, for its four main pools
wonders.summary: A wild Zambezi floodplain of oxbow pools and ana-tree woodland, where elephants stand on their hind legs to reach the branches.
wonders.uniqueness: A UNESCO natural World Heritage Site (1984, with Sapi and Chewore). One of the few parks in Africa where guided walking among big game is permitted.

media.note: Boswell — the bull elephant famous for standing on his hind legs

wonders.name: Hwange National Park
wonders.summary: Zimbabwe's largest park: Kalahari sandveld, teak forest and pans, home to one of Africa's largest elephant populations.
wonders.uniqueness: Life at Hwange gathers around its waterholes. In the dry season, herds of hundreds of elephants come to them at dusk.

media.note: Stand-in: elephant herd in Mana Pools, until Hwange footage is added

wonders.name: Matobo Hills
wonders.summary: A sea of granite kopjes, whalebacks and balancing boulders, weathered from rock that formed over 2 billion years ago.
wonders.uniqueness: A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003. It has one of the densest concentrations of rock art in southern Africa and one of the highest densities of black eagles and rhinos.

wonders.name: Chinhoyi Caves
wonders.summary: Limestone and dolomite caverns around a collapsed sinkhole holding the Sleeping Pool, a body of water that glows an unreal cobalt blue.
wonders.uniqueness: The pool's clarity and its constant temperature of about 22 °C make it a famous cave-diving site. Its depths run past 80 m into flooded passages.

wonders.name: Mutarazi Falls
wonders.summary: A thin ribbon of water that drops off the Eastern Highlands escarpment into the Honde Valley in two tiers.
wonders.uniqueness: Zimbabwe's highest waterfall at about 762 m, often cited as the second-highest in Africa. A skywalk and zipline now hang over the drop.

wonders.name: Mount Nyangani
wonders.summary: A misty moorland plateau in Nyanga National Park and the source of rivers that flow toward both the Zambezi and the Indian Ocean.
wonders.uniqueness: The highest point in Zimbabwe. Local lore holds that the mountain 'swallows' hikers, and its fast-changing mist has made that legend very easy to believe.

wonders.name: Chimanimani Mountains
wonders.summary: Jagged white quartzite peaks, crystal streams and hidden caves straddling the Mozambique border.
wonders.uniqueness: A botanical hotspot with many plant species found nowhere else on Earth. The quartzite gives the range a pale, almost lunar glow at sunrise.

media.note: No openly licensed footage or photos of the Zimbabwe side yet

wonders.name: Chilojo Cliffs, Gonarezhou
wonders.summary: Banded red-and-ochre sandstone cliffs rising high above the Runde River in Gonarezhou National Park.
wonders.uniqueness: Iconic of Zimbabwe's southeast lowveld, the cliffs blaze crimson at sunset. They're part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park, which links Zimbabwe, South Africa and Mozambique.

wonders.name: Epworth Balancing Rocks
wonders.summary: Granite boulders stacked in impossible-looking towers just outside Harare, shaped by millions of years of weathering.
wonders.uniqueness: They once appeared on Zimbabwe's banknotes, a natural sculpture garden that seems to defy gravity.

wonders.name: Great Zimbabwe
wonders.summary: The stone capital of a southern African kingdom that flourished from the 11th to the 15th century: dry-stone granite walls curving across a hilltop, a valley and the vast Great Enclosure.
wonders.uniqueness: A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986 and often described as the largest ancient stone structure south of the Sahara. The nation takes its name from it, and the soapstone Zimbabwe Bird found here flies on the national flag.

wonders.name: Flame Lily
wonders.summary: Zimbabwe’s national flower: a climbing lily whose swept-back petals flicker from gold to scarlet like a flame.
wonders.uniqueness: Specially protected under the Parks and Wildlife Act — wild flame lilies may not be picked or sold without a permit. It grows in woodland and on granite kopjes nationwide; this pin is a representative point near Harare.

wonders.name: Cave Squeaker
wonders.summary: A tiny frog, about 25 mm long, known only from caves, sinkholes and montane grassland around 1,500 m on the western slopes of the Chimanimani Mountains.
wonders.uniqueness: Critically Endangered and lost to science for 54 years: first collected in 1962, it was rediscovered in December 2016 by a Natural History Museum of Zimbabwe team who followed a call they had never heard before.

media.note: No openly licensed footage or photos yet — a living swarm stands in

wonders.name: Khami Ruins
wonders.summary: The dry-stone capital of the Torwa state, which rose as Great Zimbabwe declined: terraced granite platforms stepping down a hillside 22 km from Bulawayo.
wonders.uniqueness: A UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1986, famed for chequer and chevron patterns built into its walls, including the longest decorated wall in the region. Finds of Ming porcelain, Rhineland stoneware and Spanish porcelain show how far its trade reached.

wonders.name: Lake Kariba
wonders.summary: A vast reservoir on the Zambezi, shared with Zambia: drowned forests, islands and hippo-lined shores stretching to the horizon.
wonders.uniqueness: Filled between 1958 and 1963 behind the 128 m Kariba Dam, it is the world’s largest man-made reservoir by volume. Its creation displaced about 57,000 Tonga people, and Operation Noah rescued around 6,000 large animals from the rising water.

media.note: Original footage by Edward Mundondo: the lake from Kariba Heights, hippos on the shore, and the shoreline by boat.

wonders.name: Okavango Delta
wonders.summary: A river that never reaches the sea: the Okavango fans out across the Kalahari into a vast inland delta, flooding at the height of the dry season.
wonders.uniqueness: Inscribed in 2014 as the 1,000th World Heritage Site. Its flood comes down from the Angolan highlands months after the rains, drawing one of Africa’s great concentrations of wildlife into the desert.

wonders.name: Tsodilo Hills
wonders.summary: Four quartzite hills rising out of the Kalahari, holding more than 4,500 rock paintings within about 10 km².
wonders.uniqueness: Sometimes called the “Louvre of the Desert”, the hills are still revered by the San and Hambukushu as a place of ancestral spirits. World Heritage Site since 2001.

wonders.name: Chobe National Park
wonders.summary: Botswana’s first national park, where the Chobe River pulls enormous herds down to drink in the dry season.
wonders.uniqueness: Known for one of the largest elephant concentrations in Africa; tens of thousands gather along the riverfront and the Linyanti in the dry months.

media.note: Buffalo herd filmed along the Chobe and Victoria Falls corridor.

wonders.name: Makgadikgadi Pans
wonders.summary: The dry bed of an ancient super-lake: salt flats so wide and white they read as sky from the air.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the largest salt-pan systems on Earth. After good rains it floods shallowly, flamingos breed, and zebra and wildebeest migrate across its grasslands.

wonders.name: Nxai Pan & Baines’ Baobabs
wonders.summary: A fossil lake bed of short grass and acacia islands, home to the baobab grove the artist Thomas Baines painted in 1862.
wonders.uniqueness: Part of the Makgadikgadi system; in the rains zebra and springbok gather on its grasslands, many arriving from the Chobe–Linyanti wetlands.

wonders.name: Kubu Island
wonders.summary: A granite ridge crowned with ancient baobabs, marooned in the white of Sowa Pan.
wonders.uniqueness: A sacred site and national monument: stone walls and Stone Age tools show people have gathered on this “island” in the salt for thousands of years.

wonders.name: Central Kalahari Game Reserve
wonders.summary: One of Africa’s largest reserves: fossil river valleys, pans and grass under a huge Kalahari sky.
wonders.uniqueness: Created in 1961 for both wildlife and the San who live there. After rain, Deception Valley’s ancient riverbed draws springbok, gemsbok and black-maned Kalahari lions.

wonders.name: Gcwihaba Caves
wonders.summary: A dolomite cave in the dry north-west Kalahari, hung with stalactites and home to bat colonies.
wonders.uniqueness: Its formations grew when the Kalahari was far wetter, so the cave is an archive of the region’s past climate.

media.note: No openly licensed footage or photos found yet — swarm only.

wonders.name: Devil’s Claw
wonders.summary: A Kalahari creeper with magenta trumpet flowers and hooked fruit that hitch rides on passing hooves.
wonders.uniqueness: Its storage roots are a traditional medicine now traded worldwide as an anti-inflammatory, so wild harvesting is regulated. The pin is a representative point from GBIF records.

media.note: Photos from Namibia and a herbarium specimen — no open Botswana photo yet.

wonders.name: Plains Zebra
wonders.summary: Botswana’s national animal: zebras support the national coat of arms, and the flag’s black-and-white band echoes their stripes.
wonders.uniqueness: Each year zebras trek between the Chobe–Linyanti wetlands and Nxai Pan, a round trip of about 500 km that is often cited as Africa’s longest recorded land-mammal migration.

wonders.name: Maloti-Drakensberg Park
wonders.summary: A basalt wall rising above 3,000 m along the Lesotho border: the highest part of Southern Africa’s Great Escarpment.
wonders.uniqueness: A mixed natural and cultural World Heritage Site (2000, extended into Lesotho in 2013). Its caves and shelters hold the largest concentration of rock paintings in Africa south of the Sahara.

images.credit: Darren Glanville from Acle, Norfolk, UK
Darren Glanville from Acle, Norfolk, UK

wonders.name: Table Mountain
wonders.summary: Cape Town’s flat-topped sandstone mountain, often draped in a “tablecloth” of cloud pouring off its summit.
wonders.uniqueness: Part of the Cape Floral Region World Heritage Site and one of the New 7 Wonders of Nature. Its slopes hold an exceptional density of fynbos species.

wonders.name: Robben Island
wonders.summary: A low island in Table Bay used for nearly four centuries as a place of banishment, imprisonment and isolation.
wonders.uniqueness: Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 prison years here. World Heritage Site since 1999, as a symbol of the triumph of the human spirit over oppression.

wonders.name: Vredefort Dome
wonders.summary: The eroded core of the oldest and largest known impact structure on Earth, struck about two billion years ago.
wonders.uniqueness: The original crater is estimated at 170–300 km across. What remains is a ring of hills around the town of Vredefort, World Heritage Site since 2005.

wonders.name: Cradle of Humankind
wonders.summary: Limestone caves north-west of Johannesburg that have yielded a large share of the world’s early hominin fossils.
wonders.uniqueness: Home of “Mrs Ples” and “Little Foot” at Sterkfontein and Homo naledi at Rising Star. Part of the Fossil Hominid Sites World Heritage Site (1999, extended in 2005 to Taung and Makapan).

wonders.name: Richtersveld Cultural and Botanical Landscape
wonders.summary: A rugged mountain desert where Nama herders still move with the seasons, carrying portable rush-mat houses.
wonders.uniqueness: World Heritage Site since 2007 for a semi-nomadic pastoral way of life that is centuries old, set among one of the richest succulent floras on Earth.

wonders.name: Cape Floral Region
wonders.summary: The smallest and richest of the world’s six floral kingdoms, packed into the mountains of the south-western Cape.
wonders.uniqueness: Less than 0.5% of Africa’s area, yet nearly 20% of its flora, and about 69% of its ~9,000 plant species grow nowhere else. 13 protected clusters; this pin marks the Cederberg.

media.note: Photos from the Cederberg cluster of the property.

wonders.name: Tugela Falls
wonders.summary: A ribbon of water leaping off the Drakensberg Amphitheatre in a chain of free-falling drops.
wonders.uniqueness: With a total drop of about 948 m, it vies with Venezuela’s Angel Falls as the world’s tallest waterfall; some measurements rank it first.

wonders.name: iSimangaliso Wetland Park
wonders.summary: About 280 km of coast, coral reefs, forested dunes, lakes and swamps on the KwaZulu-Natal coast.
wonders.uniqueness: World Heritage Site since 1999. In 2025 it was extended across the border to include Mozambique’s Maputo National Park, forming one transboundary site.

wonders.name: Augrabies Falls
wonders.summary: The Orange River thunders into a granite gorge in the middle of the Northern Cape desert.
wonders.uniqueness: The main fall drops about 56 m into a gorge roughly 18 km long, protected by Augrabies Falls National Park since 1966.

wonders.name: Blyde River Canyon
wonders.summary: A 26 km sandstone canyon on the Drakensberg escarpment, with the Three Rondavels standing over the Blyde River.
wonders.uniqueness: Often called one of the largest “green canyons” on Earth for its subtropical forest. At Bourke’s Luck the Treur and Blyde rivers have scoured giant potholes.

wonders.name: Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
wonders.summary: A sandstone hill above the Limpopo–Shashe confluence, seat of the first known kingdom in Southern Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Between about 1220 and 1290 it grew rich on gold and ivory traded to the Indian Ocean; the famous golden rhino came from a royal grave here. Its decline preceded the rise of Great Zimbabwe. World Heritage Site since 2003.

wonders.name: Barberton Makhonjwa Mountains
wonders.summary: Some of the oldest and best-preserved volcanic and sedimentary rocks on Earth, 3.6–3.25 billion years old.
wonders.uniqueness: They preserve debris from meteorite impacts and some of the earliest traces of life, a window onto the young Earth. World Heritage Site since 2018.

media.note: Satellite views (NASA Landsat 8, ESA Sentinel-2).

wonders.name: ǂKhomani Cultural Landscape
wonders.summary: Red Kalahari dunes on the Botswana and Namibia borders, home to the ǂKhomani San and their traditions.
wonders.uniqueness: Inscribed in 2017 for a San way of life, and a knowledge of the desert, that run from the Stone Age to the present.

media.note: Filmed in the Nossob riverbed, Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, which the cultural landscape lies within.

wonders.name: Nelson Mandela Legacy Sites
wonders.summary: Fourteen places that tell South Africa’s 20th-century struggle for freedom. This pin marks the Union Buildings in Pretoria.
wonders.uniqueness: Inscribed in 2024 as “Human Rights, Liberation and Reconciliation”; components include Sharpeville, Walter Sisulu Square and Mqhekezweni, where Mandela grew up.

media.note: Union Buildings, Pretoria — one of 14 components.

wonders.name: Pleistocene Occupation Sites
wonders.summary: Coastal and inland caves preserving a record of modern human behaviour that reaches back about 162,000 years.
wonders.uniqueness: Pinnacle Point (this pin), Diepkloof and Sibhudu hold early evidence of ochre processing, engraved patterns, shell beads and advanced weapons. World Heritage Site since 2024.

wonders.name: Kruger National Park
wonders.summary: One of Africa’s great game reserves, stretching about 360 km along the Mozambique border.
wonders.uniqueness: First protected as the Sabi Game Reserve in 1898, it is now part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park with Mozambique and Zimbabwe.

media.note: Plains zebra coming to drink, H1-3 road south of Satara.

wonders.name: King Protea
wonders.summary: South Africa’s national flower, with the largest flower head of any protea: up to about 30 cm across.
wonders.uniqueness: A fire-adapted fynbos shrub that resprouts from a thick underground stem after veld fires. The pin is a representative point from GBIF records in the Western Cape.

wonders.name: African Penguin
wonders.summary: Africa’s only penguin, braying like a donkey on the granite of the Cape coast.
wonders.uniqueness: Classified as Critically Endangered by the IUCN in 2024 after decades of steep decline. Colonies such as Stony Point at Betty’s Bay (this pin) are closely protected.

media.note: Wild colony at Betty’s Bay.

wonders.name: Namib Sand Sea
wonders.summary: The only coastal desert in the world with vast dune fields shaped by fog: a sea of sand covering more than 3 million hectares.
wonders.uniqueness: Some dunes around Sossusvlei rise over 300 m, and beetles and plants harvest Atlantic fog to drink. World Heritage Site since 2013.

media.note: Sossusvlei, inside the Namib Sand Sea.

wonders.name: Twyfelfontein
wonders.summary: One of the largest concentrations of rock engravings in Africa: more than 2,000 figures cut into sandstone around a desert spring.
wonders.uniqueness: Rhinos, giraffes, lions and human footprints, carved by hunter-gatherers over thousands of years. Namibia’s first World Heritage Site (2007).

wonders.name: Etosha National Park
wonders.summary: A salt pan white as chalk, ringed by waterholes where elephant, rhino and lion gather in the dry season.
wonders.uniqueness: Proclaimed a game reserve in 1907, it is one of Africa’s oldest protected areas. The pan alone covers about 4,800 km².

wonders.name: Fish River Canyon
wonders.summary: Africa’s largest canyon: about 160 km long and up to roughly 550 m deep, cut by the Fish River through Namibia’s southern plateau.
wonders.uniqueness: A five-day hiking trail follows the canyon floor, and hot springs at Ai-Ais sit at its southern end.

wonders.name: Epupa Falls
wonders.summary: The Kunene River splinters into dozens of channels and tumbles through a series of falls on the Angola border.
wonders.uniqueness: The falls spread over about 1.5 km, framed by baobabs and makalani palms in the homeland of the Himba.

wonders.name: Brandberg
wonders.summary: Namibia’s highest mountain, a granite massif that glows red at sunset.
wonders.uniqueness: Its summit, Königstein, reaches about 2,573 m, and its ravines hold thousands of rock paintings, including the famous “White Lady”.

images.credit: Greg Willis from Denver, CO, USA

wonders.name: Spitzkoppe
wonders.summary: Bald granite peaks more than 120 million years old, rising about 700 m out of the Namib plains: the “Matterhorn of Namibia”.
wonders.uniqueness: Rock arches and shelters at its base, such as Bushman’s Paradise, hold San paintings.

wonders.name: Skeleton Coast
wonders.summary: Fog, surf and shipwrecks: a coast where dunes run straight into the cold Atlantic.
wonders.uniqueness: The Benguela Current breeds dense fog, and desert-adapted lions and brown hyenas forage along the shore. National park since 1971.

wonders.name: Dragon’s Breath Cave
wonders.summary: A cave hiding the world’s largest known non-subglacial underground lake.
wonders.uniqueness: Found in 1986, the lake covers almost 2 hectares of crystal-clear water, and the cave reaches a total depth of about 205 m. It is named for the warm, moist air that breathes out of its entrance.

media.note: A 1986 survey sketch of the cave; no open photo of the lake yet.

wonders.name: Welwitschia
wonders.summary: A desert plant with only two leaves, which keep growing for its whole life and are shredded by wind into a tangle.
wonders.uniqueness: Individuals are estimated to live well over 1,000 years, drinking Atlantic fog. It appears on Namibia’s coat of arms. This pin marks the Welwitschia Plains near Swakopmund.

wonders.name: Gemsbok
wonders.summary: A desert antelope with rapier-straight horns; a pair support Namibia’s coat of arms.
wonders.uniqueness: Built for drought, it can go long periods without drinking, getting water from melons and roots and letting its body heat rise by day to save water.

media.note: Stand-in: filmed in the Kgalagadi (South Africa); no open Namibian clip yet.

wonders.name: Lake Malawi National Park
wonders.summary: Clear water and granite islands at the lake’s southern tip, alive with hundreds of cichlid species found nowhere else.
wonders.uniqueness: World Heritage Site since 1984, created mainly to protect fish. Its cichlids are a textbook case of evolution, often compared to Darwin’s finches. The lake is shared with Mozambique (Lago Niassa) and Tanzania.

wonders.name: Mount Mulanje Cultural Landscape
wonders.summary: A granite massif rising abruptly from tea estates; its summit, Sapitwa, is the highest point in Malawi.
wonders.uniqueness: Inscribed in 2025 as a cultural landscape: the Yao, Mang’anja and Lhomwe hold the mountain sacred as home of deities, spirits and ancestors.

wonders.name: Chongoni Rock-Art Area
wonders.summary: Forested granite hills in central Malawi with 127 painted rock sites, the densest cluster of rock art in Central Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: The paintings run from Late Stone Age hunter-gatherers to Chewa farmers, whose rituals still connect to the shelters. World Heritage Site since 2006.

wonders.name: Nyika Plateau
wonders.summary: A rolling grassland plateau above 2,000 m in Malawi’s largest national park.
wonders.uniqueness: In the rains its grasslands flower with around 200 orchid species, while roan antelope and zebra graze between patches of montane forest.

wonders.name: Zomba Plateau
wonders.summary: A flat-topped massif above Malawi’s old colonial capital, cloaked in forest, streams and waterfalls.
wonders.uniqueness: At about 2,087 m, its viewpoints look out toward Lake Chilwa and Mulanje on clear days.

wonders.name: Liwonde National Park
wonders.summary: The Shire River winds through palm savanna crowded with hippos and crocodiles.
wonders.uniqueness: Managed by African Parks since 2015, which has brought back cheetahs and lions.

wonders.name: Lake Chilwa
wonders.summary: A shallow, slightly salty lake ringed by swamps and floodplains near the Mozambique border.
wonders.uniqueness: A Ramsar wetland and UNESCO biosphere reserve. It has dried out completely several times and refilled, yet still supports a major fishery.

wonders.name: Majete Wildlife Reserve
wonders.summary: Emptied by poaching in the 1980s, Majete is again home to the Big Five.
wonders.uniqueness: Since African Parks took over management in 2003, thousands of animals have been reintroduced, including elephant, black rhino, lion and leopard.

wonders.name: Mulanje Cedar
wonders.summary: Malawi’s national tree: a towering cypress found only on Mount Mulanje.
wonders.uniqueness: Critically Endangered after logging and fires, with a replanting effort under way on the massif. Trees can reach 40–50 m.

wonders.name: Zebra Mbuna
wonders.summary: A rock-dwelling cichlid of Lake Malawi, one of hundreds of mbuna species that evolved within a single lake.
wonders.uniqueness: Mbuna graze algae from the rocks. Their colours and fast-forming species make Lake Malawi a living laboratory of evolution. The pin is a representative point from GBIF records.

media.note: Aquarium specimens — no open underwater footage from the lake yet.

wonders.name: South Luangwa National Park
wonders.summary: An oxbow-laced river valley famous as the birthplace of the walking safari.
wonders.uniqueness: The Luangwa’s lagoons hold some of Africa’s densest hippo populations, and the valley is renowned for leopards and Thornicroft’s giraffe.

images.credit: Geoff Gallice from Gainesville, FL, USA

wonders.name: Kafue National Park
wonders.summary: Zambia’s largest national park, about 22,400 km² of floodplain and miombo woodland.
wonders.uniqueness: In the north the Busanga Plains flood each year and draw red lechwe, puku and lions; it is one of the largest parks in Africa.

wonders.name: Lower Zambezi National Park
wonders.summary: Elephants wade between islands on the Zambezi’s north bank, facing Zimbabwe’s Mana Pools.
wonders.uniqueness: A private presidential reserve until 1983, which spared it from heavy hunting. With Mana Pools it forms one of Africa’s great river wildernesses.

wonders.name: Kalambo Falls
wonders.summary: A single drop of about 235 m on the Tanzania border, among the tallest uninterrupted waterfalls in Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: The site is also a key archaeological record: in 2023 researchers reported the oldest known wooden structure here, at least 476,000 years old.

wonders.name: Liuwa Plain National Park
wonders.summary: A vast floodplain grassland in Barotseland, with Africa’s second-largest wildebeest migration.
wonders.uniqueness: Protected since the 19th century, when the Litunga (king of the Lozi) made it a royal hunting ground. Hyenas, lions and wild dogs follow the herds.

wonders.name: Bangweulu Wetlands
wonders.local_name: Bangweulu: “where the water meets the sky”
wonders.summary: A shallow lake and huge swamp on northern Zambia’s plateau, flat to the horizon.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the best places on Earth to see the shoebill, and home to tens of thousands of endemic black lechwe.

wonders.name: Ngonye Falls
wonders.summary: The Zambezi pours over a horseshoe of rock in western Zambia, a few hundred kilometres upstream of Victoria Falls.
wonders.uniqueness: A broad crescent of cascades in Sioma Ngwezi country, a quieter preview of the river that later becomes Mosi-oa-Tunya.

wonders.name: Nsumbu & Lake Tanganyika
wonders.summary: Zambia’s stretch of Lake Tanganyika: sandy bays, cliffs and clear water at the south end of one of the world’s deepest lakes.
wonders.uniqueness: Lake Tanganyika is the second-deepest and second-oldest lake on Earth, and its cichlids evolved in parallel with Lake Malawi’s.

wonders.name: Kundalila Falls
wonders.summary: A clear stream drops about 60 m off the Muchinga escarpment.
wonders.uniqueness: Rock pools at the top sit on the edge of the escarpment, with wide views over miombo woodland.

wonders.name: Zambezi Teak
wonders.summary: A hardwood of the Kalahari sands that once formed dense forests across western Zambia.
wonders.uniqueness: Its heavy red timber went into railway sleepers and parquet floors across the region, and much of the old forest has been logged. The pin is a representative point near Sesheke.

wonders.name: Kasanka Bat Migration
wonders.summary: Every November, an estimated 8–10 million straw-coloured fruit bats descend on a small patch of swamp forest in Kasanka National Park.
wonders.uniqueness: Often called the largest mammal migration on Earth by numbers. The bats stay for about two months, feasting on wild fruit.

wonders.name: Island of Mozambique
wonders.summary: A coral island off the northern coast that gave the country its name and was the capital of Portuguese East Africa until 1898.
wonders.uniqueness: World Heritage Site since 1991. Its stone town and macuti (palm-thatch) town show centuries of Swahili, Arab, Indian and Portuguese exchange; the Chapel of Nossa Senhora do Baluarte (1522) is often cited as the oldest European building in the southern hemisphere.

wonders.name: Gorongosa National Park
wonders.summary: A rift-valley park of floodplains, lakes and woodland, reborn after civil war nearly wiped out its wildlife.
wonders.uniqueness: A long-term restoration partnership has helped large-mammal numbers climb from a few thousand to many tens of thousands. Rain-forested Mount Gorongosa feeds its rivers.

wonders.name: Bazaruto Archipelago
wonders.summary: Islands of towering dunes and turquoise shallows off Vilankulo.
wonders.uniqueness: A national park since 1971. Its seagrass meadows shelter Mozambique’s largest remaining dugong population, along with sea turtles and coral reefs.

wonders.name: Quirimbas Archipelago
wonders.summary: A chain of coral islands and mangroves in Cabo Delgado, including Ibo’s old Swahili-Portuguese town.
wonders.uniqueness: The national park (2002) protects the southern islands and a large mainland area, and is also a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

wonders.name: Mount Mabu
wonders.summary: About 7,000 ha of old-growth rainforest on a remote mountain, spotted by scientists on Google Earth in 2005.
wonders.uniqueness: Expeditions from 2008 found species new to science, including butterflies, chameleons and a snake. It is one of the largest mid-altitude rainforests in southern Africa.

images.credit: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems, U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team

wonders.name: Mount Namuli
wonders.summary: A granite dome rising to 2,419 m: Mozambique’s second-highest mountain and a “sky island” of endemic life.
wonders.uniqueness: Its montane grassland and forest patches shelter species found nowhere else, such as the Namuli apalis and Vincent’s bush squirrel.

wonders.name: Maputo National Park
wonders.summary: Coastal lakes, swamps and forested dunes on Maputo Bay, where turtles nest on the beaches.
wonders.uniqueness: Since 2025 it has been part of the transboundary World Heritage Site “iSimangaliso Wetland Park and Maputo National Park”, shared with South Africa.

wonders.name: African Blackwood
wonders.summary: A small, slow-growing tree with near-black heartwood: the wood of clarinets, oboes and bagpipes.
wonders.uniqueness: Much of the world’s supply comes from Mozambique and Tanzania. Trees take 60 years or more to mature, and the species is rated Near Threatened. The pin is a representative point from GBIF records.

media.note: Stand-ins: a tree in Tanzania and flowers in Pretoria NBG.

wonders.name: Dugong
wonders.summary: A gentle sea cow grazing the seagrass in the bay behind the Bazaruto islands.
wonders.uniqueness: About 120 animals here form the largest remnant dugong population in Mozambique, often described as the last viable one on East Africa’s coast.

media.note: Stand-in: filmed in the Red Sea (Egypt); no open Bazaruto footage yet.

wonders.name: Al Qal'a of Beni Hammad
wonders.summary: The ruined first capital of the Hammadid dynasty, founded in 1007 in the Hodna mountains.
wonders.uniqueness: Its great mosque, with a 25 m minaret, is among the oldest in Algeria. The city was abandoned in 1090 under threat from the Banu Hilal. World Heritage Site since 1980.

wonders.name: Tassili n'Ajjer
wonders.summary: A sandstone plateau of rock forests and canyons holding more than 15,000 prehistoric paintings and engravings.
wonders.uniqueness: The art records a green Sahara of hippos, cattle herders and dancing figures. The plateau also shelters the last wild Saharan cypresses. A mixed (cultural and natural) World Heritage Site since 1982.
