wonders.name: Djémila
wonders.summary: A Roman mountain town at about 900 m, with forum, temples, basilicas and arches laid out on a narrow ridge.
wonders.uniqueness: Its plan shows how Roman builders adapted their grid to steep terrain. Its museum walls are covered with mosaics found on site. World Heritage Site since 1982.

wonders.name: Tipasa
wonders.summary: Punic, Roman, early Christian and Byzantine ruins on the shore west of Algiers.
wonders.uniqueness: A trading post turned Roman colony, with basilicas and a royal Numidian-Mauretanian mausoleum nearby. World Heritage Site since 1982.

wonders.name: Timgad
wonders.summary: A Roman garrison town founded by Trajan around 100 CE, with an almost perfect grid of streets.
wonders.uniqueness: Often called the “Pompeii of North Africa”. Its Arch of Trajan, theatre and library survived because sand buried the city. World Heritage Site since 1982.

wonders.name: Kasbah of Algiers
wonders.summary: The old hillside medina of Algiers, a maze of whitewashed houses, mosques and Ottoman palaces dropping to the sea.
wonders.uniqueness: Built over ancient Icosium and shaped by the Zirids and Ottomans. Its alleys were a stronghold of the independence struggle. World Heritage Site since 1992.

wonders.name: M'Zab Valley
wonders.summary: Five fortified ksour built from the 10th–11th century by the Ibadi Mozabites in a Saharan valley.
wonders.uniqueness: Its simple, functional earthen architecture, with each town climbing to a mosque minaret, has influenced modern architects. World Heritage Site since 1982.

wonders.name: Hoggar Mountains
wonders.summary: A volcanic highland in the central Sahara, with basalt organ-pipe peaks rising to Mount Tahat at about 2,900 m.
wonders.uniqueness: Homeland of the Kel Ahaggar Tuareg. Sunrise at Assekrem, where Charles de Foucauld built his hermitage, is one of the Sahara’s great views.

media.credit: Sofiane Mohammed Amri (photo), Nabin K. Sapkota (video)

wonders.name: Djurdjura National Park
wonders.summary: Limestone peaks of the Tell Atlas in Kabylie, with cedar forests and deep karst caves.
wonders.uniqueness: Home to Barbary macaques, and to Anou Boussouil, one of the deepest known caves in Africa. Also a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

wonders.name: El Kala National Park
wonders.summary: Lakes, cork-oak forest and dunes on the Mediterranean at the Tunisian border.
wonders.uniqueness: Its lakes Tonga and Oubeïra are Ramsar wetlands for wintering waterbirds; the park is also a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

wonders.name: Grand Erg Oriental
wonders.summary: A great sea of dunes in the Algerian Sahara, spilling into Tunisia.
wonders.uniqueness: Its star dunes and linear ridges cover roughly 600 km by 200 km, with dunes over 100 m high in places.

wonders.name: Fennec Fox
wonders.summary: The smallest fox, with the largest ears for its size: a nocturnal hunter of the Sahara’s sands. Algeria’s national animal.
wonders.uniqueness: Its ears shed desert heat and hear insects underground; furry soles let it run on hot sand. It can go long periods without free water. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Atlas Cedar
wonders.summary: A tall cedar of the Atlas and Aurès mountains, with blue-green needles and layered branches.
wonders.uniqueness: Found only in Morocco and Algeria, where forests are shrinking with drought and grazing. It is listed as Endangered. The pin is a representative point in the Aurès.

wonders.name: Abu Mena
wonders.summary: The ruins of a Late Antique Christian pilgrimage town built over the tomb of Saint Menas, south-west of Alexandria.
wonders.uniqueness: Pilgrims carried home small flasks of its holy water, found across the Mediterranean world. Rising groundwater from irrigation has put the site on the List in Danger since 2001.

wonders.name: Ancient Thebes and its Necropolis
wonders.summary: The New Kingdom capital at Luxor: the temples of Karnak and Luxor on the east bank, the Valley of the Kings on the west.
wonders.uniqueness: Karnak is one of the largest religious complexes ever built. Across the river lie royal tombs such as Tutankhamun’s and the mortuary temple of Hatshepsut. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Historic Cairo
wonders.summary: The medieval city of mosques, madrasas, hammams and fountains, founded in the 10th century.
wonders.uniqueness: Al-Azhar, one of the world’s oldest universities, and the Citadel of Saladin are part of it. Often called the “city of a thousand minarets”. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Nubian Monuments from Abu Simbel to Philae
wonders.summary: The temples of Ramesses II at Abu Simbel and of Isis at Philae, among others, on the Nile in Nubia.
wonders.uniqueness: In the 1960s an international UNESCO campaign cut Abu Simbel into blocks and moved it uphill, away from the rising waters of Lake Nasser. That campaign inspired the World Heritage Convention.

wonders.name: Memphis and its Necropolis: Giza to Dahshur
wonders.summary: The Old Kingdom capital and its pyramid fields: Giza, Saqqara, Abusir and Dahshur.
wonders.uniqueness: The Great Pyramid of Khufu is the only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World still standing. Djoser’s step pyramid at Saqqara is among the oldest large stone buildings. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Saint Catherine Area
wonders.summary: The 6th-century Orthodox monastery of Saint Catherine at the foot of Mount Sinai.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the oldest working Christian monasteries, built under Justinian. The mountain is sacred to Christianity, Islam and Judaism. World Heritage Site since 2002.

wonders.name: Wadi Al-Hitan
wonders.summary: Hundreds of fossil whale skeletons lying in the desert of the Fayoum, from a sea that covered it 40 million years ago.
wonders.uniqueness: The fossils of Basilosaurus and Dorudon still have small hind legs, showing how whales evolved from land mammals. Egypt’s first natural World Heritage Site (2005).

wonders.name: White Desert
wonders.summary: Chalk towers and “mushroom” rocks sculpted by wind in the Farafra Depression.
wonders.uniqueness: The chalk is made of tiny marine fossils. In moonlight the formations glow like snow; the area has been protected since 2002.

wonders.name: Ras Muhammad National Park
wonders.summary: The southern tip of Sinai, where the Gulfs of Suez and Aqaba meet over coral reefs.
wonders.uniqueness: Egypt’s first national park (1983). Its reef walls drop hundreds of metres, and its mangroves are among the most northerly in the world.

wonders.name: Gilf Kebir
wonders.summary: A vast sandstone plateau in Egypt’s far south-west, one of the most remote places in the Sahara.
wonders.uniqueness: Its caves hold the “Cave of Swimmers” and the Cave of the Beasts, with painted figures from a wetter Sahara.

wonders.name: Siwa Oasis
wonders.summary: A palm and olive oasis near the Libyan border, with salt lakes and a town of mud-and-salt kershef.
wonders.uniqueness: Its Oracle of Amun was consulted by Alexander the Great. The Siwi people speak a Berber language, unlike the rest of Egypt.

wonders.name: Steppe Eagle
wonders.summary: A large migrating eagle that funnels through Suez and Sinai each spring and autumn, between Eurasia and East Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: The Red Sea flyway carries hundreds of thousands of raptors over Egypt. The steppe eagle has declined sharply and is listed as Endangered. The pin is at Suez.

wonders.name: Blue Lotus
wonders.summary: A water lily of the Nile that opens at morning and closes at dusk, painted on tomb walls for thousands of years.
wonders.uniqueness: Ancient Egyptians linked it with the sun and rebirth; it appears in temple art and on Tutankhamun’s funerary objects. The pin is in the Nile Delta.

wonders.name: Rock-Art Sites of Tadrart Acacus
wonders.summary: A mountain range of dark sandstone arches near Ghat, with thousands of paintings and engravings.
wonders.uniqueness: The art spans from about 12,000 BCE to the 1st century CE, showing giraffes, elephants and later cattle and horses as the Sahara dried. World Heritage Site since 1985; on the List in Danger since 2016.

wonders.name: Cyrene
wonders.summary: A Greek colony founded about 631 BCE in the Green Mountain, later one of the great Roman cities of Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Its sanctuary of Apollo and Temple of Zeus rival those of Greece. Cyrene was famed for silphium, a medicinal plant traded until it vanished. On the List in Danger since 2016.

wonders.name: Old Town of Ghadamès
wonders.summary: An oasis town of linked mud-brick houses and covered alleys on the old caravan routes.
wonders.uniqueness: Houses have separate levels for families and rooftop walkways for women. The town stays cool in desert heat. World Heritage Site since 1986.

wonders.name: Leptis Magna
wonders.summary: One of the best-preserved Roman cities, enlarged by the emperor Septimius Severus, who was born here.
wonders.uniqueness: Its theatre, basilica, harbour and the Arch of Septimius Severus survived largely because sand covered them. On the List in Danger since 2016.

wonders.name: Sabratha
wonders.summary: A Phoenician trading post that became a Roman city on the Tripolitanian coast.
wonders.uniqueness: Its three-storey theatre, built around 190 CE, looks out to the Mediterranean. On the List in Danger since 2016.

wonders.name: Waw an Namus
wonders.summary: A black volcanic crater in the middle of the Sahara, holding small salty lakes ringed with reeds.
wonders.uniqueness: Its dark ash field stands out from space against the sand. The crater is about 4 km across, one of the most isolated volcanoes on Earth.

wonders.name: Jebel Akhdar
wonders.summary: A wooded limestone upland in Cyrenaica, the wettest part of Libya.
wonders.uniqueness: Juniper and cypress woods and fertile valleys made it the heartland of ancient Cyrene, in a country that is mostly desert.

wonders.name: Ubari Lakes
wonders.summary: Palm-fringed salt lakes among the dunes of the Ubari Sand Sea in the Fezzan.
wonders.uniqueness: Fed by ancient groundwater, the lakes are saltier than the sea. Lakes such as Gaberoun and Umm al-Maa are falling as the water table drops.

wonders.name: Barbary Sheep
wonders.summary: A sure-footed wild goat-sheep of the Sahara’s rocky massifs, with a long fringe of hair on its throat and forelegs.
wonders.uniqueness: It can live without drinking for long periods, getting water from plants. It appears in Saharan rock art. The pin is in the Acacus.

wonders.name: Pomegranate
wonders.summary: A fruit tree grown in Mediterranean gardens and oases since antiquity, with ruby seeds inside a leathery skin.
wonders.uniqueness: Cultivated across North Africa since Phoenician and Roman times; the Romans called it the “Punic apple”. The pin is a representative point near Tripoli.

wonders.name: Medina of Fez
wonders.summary: One of the largest car-free urban areas in the world, founded in the 9th century.
wonders.uniqueness: Al-Qarawiyyin, founded in 859, is often cited as the oldest continually operating university. The Chouara tannery still dyes leather in stone vats. World Heritage Site since 1981.

wonders.name: Medina of Marrakesh
wonders.summary: The red city founded by the Almoravids in 1070, with the Koutoubia minaret and the square of Jemaa el-Fnaa.
wonders.uniqueness: Jemaa el-Fnaa, with its storytellers, musicians and food stalls, helped inspire UNESCO’s list of Intangible Cultural Heritage. World Heritage Site since 1985.

wonders.name: Ksar of Aït-Ben-Haddou
wonders.summary: A fortified village of earthen kasbahs stacked up a hillside on the old caravan road from the Sahara to Marrakesh.
wonders.uniqueness: A classic example of southern Moroccan earthen architecture, and a backdrop for many films. World Heritage Site since 1987.

wonders.name: Historic City of Meknes
wonders.summary: The imperial capital of Sultan Moulay Ismail, ringed by some 40 km of walls.
wonders.uniqueness: The monumental Bab Mansour gate and vast royal granaries and stables show the scale of his 17th-century projects. World Heritage Site since 1996.

wonders.name: Volubilis
wonders.summary: A Berber and Roman city on fertile plains below the Zerhoun hills, with fine floor mosaics still in place.
wonders.uniqueness: A capital of Mauretania and a Roman frontier town; later Idris I came here to found the first Moroccan dynasty. World Heritage Site since 1997.

wonders.name: Medina of Tétouan
wonders.summary: A whitewashed medina below the Rif, rebuilt by Andalusian refugees after 1492.
wonders.uniqueness: It is one of the most complete medinas in Morocco and shows strong Andalusian influence. World Heritage Site since 1997.

wonders.name: Medina of Essaouira
wonders.summary: An 18th-century fortified port on the Atlantic, laid out by a French engineer for the sultan.
wonders.uniqueness: It blends European military design with a North African medina, and it is known for its wind, gnawa music and thuya-wood crafts. World Heritage Site since 2001.

wonders.name: Portuguese City of Mazagan
wonders.summary: A Portuguese Renaissance fortress on the Atlantic, built from 1514.
wonders.uniqueness: Its vaulted underground cistern, where light falls through a single opening onto shallow water, is the town’s best-known sight. World Heritage Site since 2004.

wonders.name: Rabat, Modern Capital and Historic City
wonders.summary: The capital on the Bou Regreg, joining the Kasbah of the Udayas and Hassan Tower with a 20th-century city plan.
wonders.uniqueness: Inscribed in 2012 for its dialogue between Arab-Muslim heritage and modern European urbanism; Hassan Tower is the unfinished minaret of a 12th-century mosque.

wonders.name: Jbel Toubkal
wonders.summary: The highest peak in North Africa, in the High Atlas south of Marrakesh.
wonders.uniqueness: At 4,167 m it is often snow-capped in winter. Berber villages in the Imlil valley are the starting point of the climb.

wonders.name: Ouzoud Falls
wonders.summary: A tiered waterfall of about 110 m dropping into the gorge of the El Abid River in the Middle Atlas.
wonders.uniqueness: Barbary macaques live in the olive groves around the falls. The name comes from the Berber word for olive.

wonders.name: Erg Chebbi
wonders.summary: A field of orange dunes near Merzouga, on the western edge of the Sahara.
wonders.uniqueness: Its dunes rise up to about 150 m. After rare rains a lake forms nearby and flamingos sometimes visit.

wonders.name: Todgha Gorge
wonders.summary: A limestone canyon in the High Atlas, with walls up to about 400 m and a gap as narrow as about 10 m.
wonders.uniqueness: The Todgha River cut through the eastern High Atlas here; the gorge is a major rock-climbing area.

wonders.name: Barbary Macaque
wonders.summary: The only wild primate north of the Sahara, living in the cedar forests of the Atlas and Rif.
wonders.uniqueness: Males help carry and care for infants, unusual among macaques. It is Endangered; Morocco’s Middle Atlas cedar forests near Azrou hold the largest population. A small introduced group lives on Gibraltar.

wonders.name: Argan Tree
wonders.summary: A thorny, drought-hardy tree of south-west Morocco whose kernels give argan oil.
wonders.uniqueness: Goats climb its branches to eat the fruit. Women’s cooperatives press the oil by hand; the argan area is a UNESCO biosphere reserve and the know-how is intangible heritage.

wonders.name: Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe
wonders.summary: The steep pyramids and royal city of the Kingdom of Kush, between the Nile and the Atbara River.
wonders.uniqueness: Meroë was a capital from the 8th century BCE to the 4th century CE, and a centre of iron-working. Its more than 200 pyramids are smaller and steeper than Egypt’s. World Heritage Site since 2011.

wonders.name: Gebel Barkal and the Sites of the Napatan Region
wonders.summary: A flat-topped sandstone mountain by the Nile, held sacred by Egyptians and Kushites as the home of Amun.
wonders.uniqueness: Its temples, palaces and the royal tombs at El-Kurru and Nuri belong to the Napatan kings who ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty. World Heritage Site since 2003.

wonders.name: Sanganeb and Dungonab Bay
wonders.summary: An isolated coral atoll and a coastal bay on Sudan’s Red Sea coast, north of Port Sudan.
wonders.uniqueness: Dungonab Bay and Mukkawar Island host dugongs, manta rays and nesting turtles. The site was inscribed as natural World Heritage in 2016.

media.note: Red Sea reef stand-in — no open footage of Sanganeb or Dungonab yet.

wonders.name: Jebel Marra
wonders.summary: A volcanic massif in Darfur rising to about 3,042 m, with crater lakes in its summit caldera.
wonders.uniqueness: The Deriba caldera holds two lakes. The mountains catch rain and stay green, with waterfalls and orchards, in an otherwise arid region.

wonders.name: Dinder National Park
wonders.summary: A savanna and floodplain park on the Ethiopian border, with oxbow lakes called mayas.
wonders.uniqueness: It is a UNESCO biosphere reserve and an important wetland for waterbirds; it connects with Ethiopia’s Alatish National Park.

wonders.name: Bayuda Desert
wonders.summary: A desert of black volcanic cones and craters inside the great bend of the Nile.
wonders.uniqueness: The Bayuda volcanic field has dozens of cinder cones and maar craters, some of them very young in geological terms.

wonders.name: Secretarybird
wonders.summary: A long-legged eagle that hunts on foot, stamping snakes and lizards to death in the grass.
wonders.uniqueness: Its kick lasts a fraction of a second and is aimed with great precision. It is on Sudan’s coat of arms, and is listed as Endangered. The pin is a representative point near Dinder.

wonders.name: Gum Arabic Tree
wonders.summary: A small thorny tree of the Sahel whose resin is gum arabic, used in food, drinks and paints.
wonders.uniqueness: Sudan’s “gum belt” in Kordofan and Darfur supplies much of the world’s gum arabic. The trees also fix nitrogen and hold back the desert. The pin is in Kordofan.

wonders.name: Amphitheatre of El Jem
wonders.summary: A 3rd-century Roman amphitheatre that could seat about 35,000 people, standing in a small town on the plain.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the largest amphitheatres of the Roman world and among the best preserved. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Archaeological Site of Carthage
wonders.summary: The Phoenician city that rivalled Rome, destroyed in 146 BCE and rebuilt as a Roman capital of Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Its round Punic military harbour, the Antonine Baths and the tophet survive among the villas of modern suburbs. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Dougga
wonders.summary: A Numidian, Punic and Roman hill town with a capitol, theatre and houses still standing over olive groves.
wonders.uniqueness: Often called the best-preserved small Roman town in North Africa. Its Libyco-Punic mausoleum is a rare monument of Numidian architecture. World Heritage Site since 1997.

images.credit: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World

wonders.name: Djerba: Testimony to a Settlement Pattern
wonders.summary: The largest island in North Africa, with scattered homesteads, mosques and synagogues among olive groves.
wonders.uniqueness: Ibadi, Sunni and Jewish communities have shared the island for centuries; the El Ghriba synagogue is one of Africa’s oldest. World Heritage Site since 2023.

wonders.name: Ichkeul National Park
wonders.summary: A lake and marshes near Bizerte that switch between fresh and salty water with the seasons.
wonders.uniqueness: Hundreds of thousands of ducks, geese and coots winter here. Dams once pushed it onto the List in Danger; it was removed in 2006 after recovery. World Heritage Site since 1980.

wonders.name: Kairouan
wonders.summary: The first Arab-Muslim city of the Maghreb, founded in 670.
wonders.uniqueness: Its Great Mosque, with a forest of reused Roman columns, became a model for mosques across the region. World Heritage Site since 1988.

wonders.name: Medina of Sousse
wonders.summary: A walled port town of the early Islamic period, with a ribat (fortified monastery) and Great Mosque.
wonders.uniqueness: The ribat, built in the 8th–9th century, guarded the coast. World Heritage Site since 1988.

wonders.name: Medina of Tunis
wonders.summary: The old city of Tunis, with some 700 monuments including palaces, mosques and madrasas.
wonders.uniqueness: From the 12th to the 16th century Tunis was among the greatest cities of the Islamic world. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Punic Town of Kerkuane
wonders.summary: The only Phoenician-Punic city to survive without being rebuilt by the Romans, on Cap Bon.
wonders.uniqueness: Abandoned around 250 BCE, it preserves house plans, streets and bathtubs from Punic daily life. World Heritage Site since 1985.

wonders.name: Village of Sidi Bou Saïd
wonders.summary: A white village with blue doors and shutters on a cliff above the Gulf of Tunis.
wonders.uniqueness: Protected by decree since 1915, the village drew painters such as Paul Klee and August Macke. Inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 2026.

wonders.name: Chott el Djerid
wonders.summary: The largest salt pan in the Sahara, a crust of salt crossed by a causeway.
wonders.uniqueness: It covers about 7,000 km². In summer heat its surface makes mirages; after rain, algae can tint pools pink.

wonders.name: Jebel ech Chambi
wonders.summary: Tunisia’s highest mountain, near Kasserine, with Aleppo pine forest on its slopes.
wonders.uniqueness: It is a national park and biosphere reserve, home to Cuvier’s gazelle and Barbary sheep.

wonders.name: Bou-Hedma National Park
wonders.summary: The last stand of pseudo-savanna with Acacia raddiana in Tunisia.
wonders.uniqueness: Scimitar-horned oryx and addax, both long gone from the wild in Tunisia, have been reintroduced here.

wonders.name: Barbary Stag
wonders.summary: Africa’s only native deer, living in the cork-oak forests along the Tunisian–Algerian border.
wonders.uniqueness: Hunted almost to extinction by the 1960s; protection in Tunisia and Algeria has helped it recover. The pin is in the Kroumirie forests.

wonders.name: Olive Tree
wonders.summary: The tree of Tunisia: tens of millions of olive trees cover the Sahel and the plains around Sfax.
wonders.uniqueness: Olives have been grown here since Phoenician times, and Tunisia is one of the world’s largest olive-oil exporters. The pin is near Sfax.

wonders.name: Dakhla Bay
wonders.summary: A long Atlantic lagoon behind a sandy peninsula, where the desert meets cold, nutrient-rich ocean.
wonders.uniqueness: Steady trade winds make it a kitesurfing destination; its shallows support oysters, seagrass and wintering shorebirds. The city of Dakhla is in the Moroccan-administered part of the disputed territory.

wonders.name: Saguia el-Hamra
wonders.summary: A long dry riverbed (wadi) running across the north of Western Sahara to the Atlantic near Laayoune.
wonders.uniqueness: It flows only after rare storms. The name, “red watercourse”, also served for the northern region of the former Spanish Sahara.

wonders.name: Guelta Zemmur
wonders.summary: A rocky desert of granite inselbergs and seasonal pools (gueltas) in the interior of Western Sahara.
wonders.uniqueness: Gueltas are rock basins that hold rainwater for months and were vital to herders and wildlife. Rock art is found across the region.

wonders.name: Dorcas Gazelle
wonders.summary: A small, pale gazelle of the Sahara that may never need to drink, getting water from plants and dew.
wonders.uniqueness: Once common across North Africa, it has declined from hunting and is listed as Vulnerable. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Umbrella Thorn Acacia
wonders.summary: A flat-topped thorn tree, often the only shade in the Saharan plains.
wonders.uniqueness: Its deep roots reach groundwater, and its pods feed camels and goats. The same species grows from the Sahara to East Africa. The pin is a representative point.

media.note: Photographed in East Africa — the same species grows across the Sahara’s edges.

wonders.name: Royal Palaces of Abomey
wonders.summary: The earthen palaces of the twelve kings of Dahomey, spread over 47 ha at the heart of Abomey.
wonders.uniqueness: Their walls carry painted bas-reliefs that record the kingdom’s history and wars. Dahomey (1600–1894) was one of the most powerful West African states. World Heritage Site since 1985.

wonders.name: W-Arly-Pendjari Complex
wonders.summary: The largest intact savanna ecosystem in West Africa, shared by Benin, Burkina Faso and Niger.
wonders.uniqueness: It holds most of the region’s remaining lions and elephants, plus cheetah, buffalo and roan antelope. The transboundary site was completed in 2017.

wonders.name: Ganvié
wonders.summary: A town of about 20,000 people built on stilts in Lake Nokoué, reached only by boat.
wonders.uniqueness: The Tofinu built it on the water around the 17th–18th century, out of reach of Dahomey’s slave-raiding warriors, whose beliefs forbade them to fight on water. Markets are held from canoes.

wonders.name: Kota Falls
wonders.summary: A waterfall and swimming pool in the Atakora hills near Natitingou.
wonders.uniqueness: The stream drops over a sandstone ledge into a deep pool, shaded by gallery forest in a dry landscape.

wonders.name: Bouche du Roy
wonders.summary: The estuary where the Mono River and the Grand-Popo lagoon meet the Gulf of Guinea.
wonders.uniqueness: Mangroves, sea-turtle beaches and fishing villages lie within a community conservation area and a transboundary UNESCO biosphere reserve with Togo.

wonders.name: Royal Python
wonders.summary: A gentle python that curls into a ball when threatened, sacred in the Vodun religion of southern Benin.
wonders.uniqueness: At Ouidah’s Temple of Pythons, dozens of royal pythons are kept as embodiments of the deity Dangbé and may roam the town at night. The pin is at Ouidah.

wonders.name: African Fan Palm
wonders.summary: A tall fan palm of West African savannas, with a bulge part-way up its trunk.
wonders.uniqueness: Its trunks resist termites and are used for building, its fruit and shoots are eaten, and its sap is tapped for palm wine. The pin is in northern Benin.

wonders.name: Ruins of Loropéni
wonders.summary: Stone walls up to 6 m high enclosing a settlement linked to the trans-Saharan gold trade.
wonders.uniqueness: The best preserved of about ten fortresses in the Lobi area; parts date to at least the 11th century. Burkina Faso’s first World Heritage Site (2009).

wonders.name: Ancient Ferrous Metallurgy Sites
wonders.summary: Five sites with furnaces, mines and slag heaps from about 2,700 years of iron-smelting.
wonders.uniqueness: The oldest, at Douroula, dates to the 8th century BCE. Smiths still hold a special place in local society. World Heritage Site since 2019.

media.note: No openly licensed photos of the furnace sites yet.

wonders.name: Royal Court of Tiébélé
wonders.summary: A Kassena royal compound of earthen houses painted by women with black, white and red geometric designs.
wonders.uniqueness: The paintings are renewed before the rainy season using earth, chalk and plant varnish. World Heritage Site since 2024.

wonders.name: Sindou Peaks
wonders.summary: A ridge of sandstone needles and towers carved by wind and rain near the Mali border.
wonders.uniqueness: The peaks are sacred to the Senoufo and a protected natural site.

wonders.name: Karfiguéla Falls
wonders.summary: A series of cascades over sandstone steps near Banfora, among mango groves.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the few permanent waterfalls in Burkina Faso, fed by the Comoé basin.

wonders.name: Nazinga Game Ranch
wonders.summary: A savanna reserve in the south known for elephants gathering at its waterholes.
wonders.uniqueness: Founded in 1979 to restore wildlife numbers, it now holds one of the densest elephant populations in West Africa.

wonders.name: Sacred Crocodiles of Sabou
wonders.summary: A crocodile of the Sahel’s pools, long confused with the Nile crocodile, held sacred in villages such as Sabou and Bazoulé.
wonders.uniqueness: It was recognised as a separate species in 2011. Villagers feed and protect the pond crocodiles, believed to carry ancestral spirits. The pin is at Sabou.

wonders.name: Néré
wonders.summary: A savanna tree with red pom-pom flowers whose fermented seeds make soumbala, a seasoning across West Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Its flowers are pollinated by fruit bats. Farmers keep néré trees standing in their fields. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Cidade Velha
wonders.summary: The first European colonial town in the tropics, founded in 1462 on Santiago island.
wonders.uniqueness: It was a hub of the Atlantic slave trade; its pillory, fortress and cathedral ruins remain. World Heritage Site since 2009.

wonders.name: Pico do Fogo
wonders.summary: An active stratovolcano rising to 2,829 m, the highest point of Cabo Verde.
wonders.uniqueness: Its last eruption, in 2014–15, buried villages in the Chã das Caldeiras crater, where people grow grapes and coffee in volcanic soil.

wonders.name: Paul Valley
wonders.summary: A deep green valley on Santo Antão, terraced with sugar cane, bananas and yams below the Cova crater.
wonders.uniqueness: Trade-wind clouds water the north-east of the island, making it far greener than the rest of the archipelago.

wonders.name: Pedra de Lume
wonders.summary: Salt pans inside an extinct volcanic crater on the island of Sal.
wonders.uniqueness: Seawater seeps into the crater and evaporates; the salt was exported from the 19th century. The brine is so dense that bathers float.

wonders.name: Viana Desert
wonders.summary: White dunes on the island of Boa Vista, built from sand blown across the ocean from the Sahara.
wonders.uniqueness: Boa Vista is one of the world’s most important nesting areas for loggerhead turtles.

wonders.name: Loggerhead Sea Turtle
wonders.summary: Thousands of loggerheads nest on Boa Vista’s beaches each summer.
wonders.uniqueness: Cabo Verde holds one of the largest loggerhead nesting populations in the world, mostly on Boa Vista. The pin is on Boa Vista’s east coast.

wonders.name: Dragon Tree
wonders.summary: An umbrella-shaped tree of the Atlantic islands that bleeds red resin, “dragon’s blood”.
wonders.uniqueness: The Cabo Verde form survives wild only on a few islands such as São Nicolau. The pin is on São Nicolau.

wonders.name: Comoé National Park
wonders.summary: One of the largest protected areas in West Africa, crossed by the Comoé River.
wonders.uniqueness: Its mosaic of savanna, gallery forest and riverine habitats once held elephants, hippos and lions. Removed from the List in Danger in 2017 after wildlife recovered.

wonders.name: Taï National Park
wonders.summary: One of the last large areas of primary Upper Guinean rainforest.
wonders.uniqueness: Its chimpanzees crack nuts with stone and wooden hammers, a tradition archaeologists have traced back over 4,000 years. Pygmy hippos live here too. World Heritage Site since 1982.

wonders.name: Historic Town of Grand-Bassam
wonders.summary: The first colonial capital of Côte d’Ivoire, with arcaded colonial houses between lagoon and sea.
wonders.uniqueness: The town shows the meeting of European and African ways of life; the N’zima village sits beside the old quarter. World Heritage Site since 2012.

wonders.name: Sudanese-style Mosques
wonders.summary: Eight small earthen mosques with timber struts and buttress towers, in towns such as Kong and Kaouara.
wonders.uniqueness: They follow a style that spread with traders from Djenné around the 14th century, and are replastered by their communities. World Heritage Site since 2021.

wonders.name: Banco National Park
wonders.summary: A primary rainforest inside the city of Abidjan.
wonders.uniqueness: Protected since 1926, it is one of the few urban rainforests in the world, with mahogany trees and a historic forestry school.

wonders.name: La Cascade, Man
wonders.summary: A forest waterfall in the mountains around Man, the “city of 18 mountains”.
wonders.uniqueness: The Dent de Man peak and liana bridges of the Dan people are nearby.

wonders.name: Assinie
wonders.summary: A narrow sand strip between the Aby lagoon and the Atlantic near the Ghana border.
wonders.uniqueness: The French first landed here in the 17th century; today its beaches and lagoon islands are a getaway from Abidjan.

wonders.name: Western Chimpanzee
wonders.summary: The chimpanzee of West Africa’s forests and savannas, famous for using tools.
wonders.uniqueness: Critically Endangered; numbers fell by about 80% between 1990 and 2014. Taï chimps crack nuts with hammers and anvils. The pin is in Taï.

wonders.name: Kola Nut
wonders.summary: A rainforest tree whose caffeine-rich nuts are shared as a sign of hospitality across West Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Kola has been traded north across the Sahara for centuries and gave its name to cola drinks. Côte d’Ivoire is a major producer. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Kunta Kinteh Island and Related Sites
wonders.summary: A small island in the Gambia River with the ruins of a fort used in the Atlantic slave trade.
wonders.uniqueness: Formerly James Island, it was renamed after Kunta Kinteh, the ancestor in Alex Haley’s “Roots”. World Heritage Site since 2003.

images.credit: Niels Elgaard Larsen; derivative by Jjtkk

wonders.name: Stone Circles of Senegambia
wonders.summary: More than 1,000 monuments of standing laterite stones along the Gambia River, in Gambia and Senegal.
wonders.uniqueness: Built from about the 3rd century BCE to the 16th century CE over burial sites; Wassu and Kerbatch are the best known. World Heritage Site since 2006.

wonders.name: River Gambia National Park
wonders.summary: Five river islands where rehabilitated chimpanzees live free, alongside hippos and crocodiles.
wonders.uniqueness: The Chimpanzee Rehabilitation Project has released orphaned chimps here since 1979; visitors watch only from boats.

media.note: Satellite view of the Baboon Islands.

wonders.name: Abuko Nature Reserve
wonders.summary: A small gallery forest near Banjul, The Gambia’s first protected area.
wonders.uniqueness: Protected since 1916 as a water catchment, it shelters red colobus, green monkeys, Nile crocodiles and over 250 bird species.

wonders.name: Tanji Bird Reserve
wonders.summary: Dunes, lagoons and the Bijol Islands on the Atlantic coast, beside a busy fishing village.
wonders.uniqueness: Established in 1993, it covers about 612 ha and records over 300 bird species, plus nesting turtles on the islands.

wonders.name: Temminck’s Red Colobus
wonders.summary: A leaf-eating monkey with a rust-red coat, found from The Gambia to north-west Guinea.
wonders.uniqueness: Colobus have no thumbs, and a stomach that ferments leaves. It is Endangered; Abuko is one of the easiest places to see it. The pin is at Abuko.

wonders.name: African Rosewood
wonders.summary: A savanna tree with red timber, now Endangered after a rosewood logging boom.
wonders.uniqueness: Trade is restricted under CITES since 2016 because illegal logging, much of it routed through Gambian ports, stripped forests in the region. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Forts and Castles of Ghana
wonders.summary: Fortified trading posts built along the Gold Coast between 1482 and 1786, including Elmina and Cape Coast castles.
wonders.uniqueness: Built by Portuguese, Dutch, Danish, Swedish, German and British traders, they held enslaved Africans in dungeons before the Atlantic crossing. World Heritage Site since 1979.

wonders.name: Asante Traditional Buildings
wonders.summary: The last surviving shrines and houses of the Asante kingdom, around Kumasi, built of earth, timber and thatch.
wonders.uniqueness: Their walls carry bold relief patterns, a vocabulary shared with Adinkra symbols. Much of old Kumasi was destroyed by the British in 1874. World Heritage Site since 1980.

wonders.name: Kakum National Park
wonders.summary: Moist tropical forest near Cape Coast, crossed by a canopy walkway 30–40 m above the ground.
wonders.uniqueness: The 350 m walkway hangs between giant trees. The forest shelters forest elephants, Diana monkeys and hundreds of bird and butterfly species.

wonders.name: Wli Falls
wonders.summary: Ghana’s highest waterfall, falling in two tiers in the forested Agumatsa hills near the Togo border.
wonders.uniqueness: Thousands of fruit bats roost in the cliffs around the lower fall.

wonders.name: Lake Bosumtwi
wonders.summary: Ghana’s only natural lake, sitting in a meteorite impact crater about 10.5 km across.
wonders.uniqueness: The crater is about 1 million years old. Sacred to the Asante, the lake may be fished only from wooden planks, not boats.

wonders.name: Mole National Park
wonders.summary: Ghana’s largest wildlife refuge, savanna woodland where elephants come to the waterholes below the motel.
wonders.uniqueness: It holds elephants, buffalo, antelope and over 300 bird species. The 15th-century Larabanga mosque stands nearby.

wonders.name: Grey Parrot
wonders.summary: A grey forest parrot with a red tail, famous for mimicking speech.
wonders.uniqueness: Trapping for the pet trade and forest loss wiped out an estimated 90–99% of Ghana’s grey parrots after 1992. The species is Endangered. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Ackee
wonders.summary: A West African tree whose red pods split open to show black seeds on creamy flesh.
wonders.uniqueness: Its name comes from the Twi word akye. Carried across the Atlantic in the slave era, it became Jamaica’s national fruit. Unripe fruit is toxic. The pin is near Kumasi.

wonders.name: Mount Nimba Strict Nature Reserve
wonders.summary: A mountain ridge rising to 1,752 m above the forest, shared by Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire.
wonders.uniqueness: Grassland summits over cloud forest hold many endemic species, including the viviparous Nimba toad. On the List in Danger since 1992 over iron-ore mining threats.

wonders.name: Fouta Djallon
wonders.summary: A highland of sandstone plateaus and waterfalls in central Guinea.
wonders.uniqueness: The Gambia and Senegal rivers rise here, and the Niger rises in Guinea’s southern highlands nearby, which is why Guinea is called the water tower of West Africa. Home of the Fula Imamate of Futa Jallon.

wonders.name: Voile de la Mariée
wonders.summary: A veil-like waterfall in the forested hills near Kindia.
wonders.uniqueness: Its spray spreads over a broad rock face, giving it its name. A popular trip from Conakry.

wonders.name: Îles de Los
wonders.summary: Volcanic islands off Conakry with palm-lined beaches.
wonders.uniqueness: Their name comes from the Portuguese “Ilhas dos Ídolos”, islands of idols. The islands are the remains of a volcanic ring complex.

wonders.name: Western Nimba Toad
wonders.summary: A tiny toad that gives birth to live young, found only in the grasslands of Mount Nimba.
wonders.uniqueness: Females carry their young for about nine months and feed them through a kind of placental secretion, one of very few frogs or toads to do so. Critically Endangered. The pin is on Mount Nimba.

images.credit: Sandberger-Loua L, Müller H, Rödel M-O
Sandberger-Loua L, Müller H, Rödel M-O

wonders.name: African Oil Palm
wonders.summary: The palm of the Guinea coast, whose orange fruit gives red palm oil.
wonders.uniqueness: Named for Guinea in its scientific name, it is now grown across the tropics and is the world’s most-used vegetable oil. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Bijagós Archipelago
wonders.summary: A delta archipelago of about 88 islands, with mangroves, mudflats and sacred forests.
wonders.uniqueness: Its tidal flats host hundreds of thousands of migrating shorebirds, green turtles nest on its beaches, and hippos live in brackish lagoons. The matrilineal Bijagó people manage many islands as sacred. World Heritage Site since 2025.

wonders.name: Cacheu River Mangroves
wonders.summary: One of the largest mangrove blocks in West Africa, along the Cacheu estuary.
wonders.uniqueness: Created as a natural park in 2000; manatees, crocodiles and many waterbirds live in its creeks.

wonders.name: Bolama
wonders.summary: An island town at the edge of the Bijagós that was the capital of Portuguese Guinea until 1941.
wonders.uniqueness: Its colonial avenues and public buildings now stand half-ruined among mango trees, a quiet record of the colonial era.

wonders.name: Saltwater Hippos of Orango
wonders.summary: Hippos that swim between islands through seawater in the Bijagós.
wonders.uniqueness: On Orango they live in freshwater lagoons but cross sea channels, an unusual behaviour for hippos. They are revered by the Bijagó. The pin is in Orango National Park.

media.note: Hippos photographed elsewhere — no open footage from Orango yet.

wonders.name: Red Mangrove
wonders.summary: A mangrove on arching stilt roots that lines the creeks of Guinea-Bissau.
wonders.uniqueness: Mangroves cover a large share of the country’s coast, sheltering fish nurseries and storing carbon. Its seeds sprout while still on the tree. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Sapo National Park
wonders.summary: Liberia’s largest protected rainforest, in Sinoe County.
wonders.uniqueness: Part of the Upper Guinean forest, one of the world’s biodiversity hotspots; it shelters pygmy hippos, forest elephants and chimpanzees.

media.note: No openly licensed photos of Sapo yet.

wonders.name: Kpatawee Falls
wonders.summary: A forest waterfall in Bong County, a favourite weekend escape from Monrovia.
wonders.uniqueness: Water tumbles over granite steps into pools surrounded by rainforest.

wonders.name: Lake Piso
wonders.summary: A large tidal lagoon in Grand Cape Mount County, separated from the sea by a sand bar.
wonders.uniqueness: Its mangroves and beaches are a proposed protected area; Pan Am flying boats used it as a base during the Second World War.

wonders.name: East Nimba Nature Reserve
wonders.summary: The Liberian side of the Nimba range, with montane forest above old iron-ore workings.
wonders.uniqueness: It protects forest linked to the Nimba World Heritage Site across the border in Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire.

wonders.name: Pygmy Hippopotamus
wonders.summary: A shy forest hippo about a tenth the weight of its river cousin, living alone in swamp forest.
wonders.uniqueness: Most of the world’s wild pygmy hippos live in Liberia. Fewer than about 2,500 remain; the species is Endangered. The pin is near Sapo.

wonders.name: Liberian Coffee
wonders.summary: A tall coffee tree from the West African forests with large, smoky-tasting beans.
wonders.uniqueness: It rescued coffee growing in Asia after leaf rust struck in the 19th century, and is still grown in Malaysia and the Philippines. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Old Towns of Djenné
wonders.summary: A mud-brick town in the inland Niger delta, crowned by the largest earthen building in the world, the Great Mosque.
wonders.uniqueness: Each year the whole town replasters the mosque in a festival called the Crépissage. Djenné-Djeno nearby is one of the oldest known cities south of the Sahara. World Heritage Site since 1988.

wonders.name: Timbuktu
wonders.summary: A desert city near the Niger that was a great centre of Islamic scholarship in the 15th and 16th centuries.
wonders.uniqueness: Its Djinguereber, Sankore and Sidi Yahia mosques and tens of thousands of manuscripts survive. Mausoleums destroyed in 2012 were rebuilt by local masons. World Heritage Site since 1988.

wonders.name: Cliff of Bandiagara
wonders.summary: A sandstone escarpment about 150 km long with Dogon villages, granaries and older Tellem cliff dwellings.
wonders.uniqueness: The cliff rises up to about 500 m above the plain. Dogon masks, dances and cosmology are tied to the landscape. A mixed World Heritage Site since 1989.

wonders.name: Tomb of Askia
wonders.summary: A 17 m pyramidal mud tower in Gao, built in 1495 by Askia Mohammed, emperor of Songhai.
wonders.uniqueness: It shows the Sudano-Sahelian style at its most monumental, bristling with wooden beams. World Heritage Site since 2004.

wonders.name: Inner Niger Delta
wonders.summary: A huge inland floodplain where the Niger spreads into lakes and channels at the Sahara’s edge.
wonders.uniqueness: At its peak the flood covers up to about 20,000 km². Millions of migratory birds winter here, and Fulani herders, Bozo fishers and Bambara farmers share its seasons.

wonders.name: Hand of Fatima
wonders.summary: Five sandstone fingers rising about 600 m above the Sahel plain near Hombori.
wonders.uniqueness: A famous big-wall climbing site. Nearby Hombori Tondo is Mali’s highest point at about 1,155 m.

wonders.name: Gouina Falls
wonders.summary: A broad, horseshoe-shaped waterfall on the Senegal River in western Mali.
wonders.uniqueness: The river spreads across a rock sill in a curtain about 15 m high and several hundred metres wide.

wonders.name: Desert Elephants of Gourma
wonders.summary: The most northerly elephants in Africa, walking a 32,000 km² circuit between waterholes in the Sahel.
wonders.uniqueness: They make one of the longest elephant migrations known, following rains and lakes such as Banzena. Local communities and anti-poaching patrols protect a few hundred animals. The pin is in the Gourma.

media.note: Elephants photographed elsewhere — no open footage from the Gourma yet.

wonders.name: Shea Tree
wonders.summary: A savanna tree whose nuts give shea butter, processed mostly by women across the Sahel.
wonders.uniqueness: Shea trees grow wild and take decades to bear fruit; the butter is used for cooking, skin care and chocolate. The pin is a representative point in southern Mali.

wonders.name: Banc d'Arguin National Park
wonders.summary: Sand dunes, islands and shallow seagrass flats where the Sahara meets the Atlantic.
wonders.uniqueness: Over two million shorebirds winter here. Imraguen fishermen still use lanchas, sailing boats, and work with dolphins to drive mullet into their nets. World Heritage Site since 1989.

wonders.name: Ancient Ksour of Ouadane, Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata
wonders.summary: Four caravan towns of the 11th–12th centuries, with stone houses, mosques and family libraries.
wonders.uniqueness: Chinguetti’s libraries still hold medieval manuscripts on law, astronomy and medicine, now threatened by advancing sand. World Heritage Site since 1996.

wonders.name: Richat Structure
wonders.local_name: Guelb er Richât · the Eye of Africa
wonders.summary: A target of concentric rock rings about 40 km wide in the Sahara, clearly visible from space.
wonders.uniqueness: Once thought to be an impact crater, it is an eroded geological dome. Astronauts have used it as a landmark since the early space missions.

images.credit: NASA/GSFC/METI/ERSDAC/JAROS and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team

wonders.name: Ben Amera
wonders.summary: A granite monolith rising about 633 m above the desert near the iron-ore railway.
wonders.uniqueness: Often described as one of the largest monoliths in the world. In 1999 sculptors carved works into the boulders of nearby Aïsha.

wonders.name: Terjit Oasis
wonders.summary: A palm-filled gorge in the Adrar with warm and cool springs.
wonders.uniqueness: Water emerges from the rock in a narrow canyon, creating shade and pools in one of the hottest regions on Earth.

wonders.name: Mediterranean Monk Seal
wonders.summary: One of the world’s rarest seals, living in sea caves on the Cap Blanc peninsula.
wonders.uniqueness: Cap Blanc holds the largest colony of the species. A toxic algal bloom killed about two-thirds of it in 1997; it has since recovered to several hundred animals. The pin is at Cap Blanc.

wonders.name: Date Palm
wonders.summary: The tree of the Saharan oases, cultivated in the Adrar for centuries.
wonders.uniqueness: During the guetna, the summer date harvest, families gather in oases such as Atar and Terjit. The pin is near Atar.

wonders.name: Aïr and Ténéré Natural Reserves
wonders.summary: The largest protected area in Africa, joining the volcanic Aïr Mountains with the dunes of the Ténéré.
wonders.uniqueness: It covers about 7.7 million ha, with Tuareg herders, rock art and relict Saharan wildlife such as addax and Barbary sheep. On the List in Danger since 1992.

wonders.name: Historic Centre of Agadez
wonders.summary: The “gateway to the desert”, a Tuareg sultanate town of earthen houses and palaces.
wonders.uniqueness: Its 27 m mud-brick minaret is the tallest of its kind in the world. Agadez grew in the 15th–16th centuries as a caravan hub. World Heritage Site since 2013.

wonders.name: Termit Massif
wonders.summary: Black sandstone ridges rising from the dunes south of the Ténéré.
wonders.uniqueness: Part of the Termit and Tin Toumma National Nature Reserve, one of the last refuges of the addax antelope and dama gazelle.

wonders.name: Djado Plateau
wonders.summary: A remote sandstone plateau in the far north-east, with abandoned ksour and rock art.
wonders.uniqueness: The ruined fortified villages of Djado and engravings of giraffes and cattle record its past; it is on Niger’s tentative list for World Heritage.

wonders.name: Niger River at Niamey
wonders.summary: The great river of West Africa curving past the capital, with rice fields and pirogues on its banks.
wonders.uniqueness: The Niger flows about 4,180 km in a great arc, from the Guinea highlands through the Sahel to the Atlantic in Nigeria.

wonders.name: West African Giraffe
wonders.summary: The last giraffes of West Africa, roaming farmland around Kouré near Niamey.
wonders.uniqueness: Only about 50 remained in 1996. Protection by villagers lifted numbers to several hundred. The pin is at Kouré.

wonders.name: Doum Palm
wonders.summary: A Sahel palm that branches into forks, unusual among palms, with gingerbread-tasting fruit.
wonders.uniqueness: Its leaves are woven into mats and baskets across the Sahel; doum fruits were placed in Egyptian tombs. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Sukur Cultural Landscape
wonders.summary: A hilltop chief’s palace, terraced fields and stone-paved paths in the Mandara Mountains.
wonders.uniqueness: Sukur was a centre of iron-smelting and its society has shaped the hill for centuries. Africa’s first cultural landscape on the World Heritage List (1999).

wonders.name: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
wonders.summary: One of the last sacred forests of the Yoruba, home of the river goddess Osun, outside Osogbo.
wonders.uniqueness: Shrines and sculptures were renewed from the 1950s by Susanne Wenger and local artists. Each August the Osun-Osogbo festival draws huge crowds. World Heritage Site since 2005.

wonders.name: Zuma Rock
wonders.summary: A granite dome rising about 300 m above the plain on the road from Abuja, the “gateway to Abuja”.
wonders.uniqueness: Rain streaks on its face are said to form a human face; the rock appears on Nigeria’s 100 naira note.

wonders.name: Yankari
wonders.summary: Savanna and gallery forest in Bauchi State, fed by the clear, warm Wikki Spring.
wonders.uniqueness: The spring stays at about 31 °C year round. Yankari holds one of West Africa’s largest remaining elephant herds.

wonders.name: Obudu Plateau
wonders.summary: A grassy plateau around 1,575 m on the Cameroon border, with a cool climate and forest gorges.
wonders.uniqueness: Montane grassland and forest here are part of the Cameroon highlands, home to rare birds and primates.

wonders.name: Erin Ijesha Waterfalls
wonders.summary: A seven-tier waterfall in the hills of Osun State.
wonders.uniqueness: Local tradition says it was discovered in 1140 by a hunter; climbers can follow the tiers up the hill.

wonders.name: Cross River Gorilla
wonders.summary: The rarest great ape in Africa, living in hill forests on the Nigeria–Cameroon border.
wonders.uniqueness: Only around 250–300 remain in small groups. Critically Endangered. The pin is near the Afi Mountain and Mbe Mountains.

wonders.name: Iroko
wonders.summary: A giant hardwood of the West African forest, sacred in Yoruba and Igbo tradition.
wonders.uniqueness: The tree is believed to house spirits, so many are left standing; its durable timber is used for boats and furniture. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Island of Gorée
wonders.summary: A small island off Dakar, a hub of the Atlantic slave trade from the 15th to the 19th century.
wonders.uniqueness: The House of Slaves and its “Door of No Return” is a place of memory and reconciliation. World Heritage Site since 1978.

wonders.name: Djoudj National Bird Sanctuary
wonders.summary: A delta wetland on the Senegal River, the first green after the Sahara for migrating birds.
wonders.uniqueness: About 1.5 million birds use it, including great white pelicans, flamingos and aquatic warblers. World Heritage Site since 1981.

wonders.name: Niokolo-Koba National Park
wonders.summary: Gallery forest and savanna along the Gambia River in south-east Senegal.
wonders.uniqueness: Home to the Derby (giant) eland, chimpanzees, lions and hippos. It came off the List in Danger in 2024 after wildlife began to recover. World Heritage Site since 1981.

wonders.name: Island of Saint-Louis
wonders.summary: A colonial island town at the mouth of the Senegal River, capital of French West Africa until 1902.
wonders.uniqueness: Its balconied houses and the Faidherbe Bridge, opened in 1897, give it a distinctive look. World Heritage Site since 2000.

wonders.name: Saloum Delta
wonders.summary: Mangrove islands, creeks and shell mounds where the Saloum meets the Atlantic.
wonders.uniqueness: 218 shell middens, some with burial tumuli, record 2,000 years of shellfish gathering. World Heritage Site since 2011.

wonders.name: Bassari Country
wonders.summary: Hill villages of the Bassari, Fula and Bedik peoples in south-east Senegal.
wonders.uniqueness: Their terraced fields, masked initiation rites and villages show cultures adapted to this upland. World Heritage Site since 2012.

wonders.name: Lac Rose
wonders.summary: A shallow salt lake that turns pink in the dry season, north-east of Dakar.
wonders.uniqueness: The colour comes from salt-loving algae (Dunaliella salina). Salt collectors gather salt from the bottom, protecting their skin with shea butter. Long the finish of the Paris–Dakar rally.

wonders.name: Dindéfelo Falls
wonders.summary: A waterfall of about 100 m dropping into a pool in the Fouta Djallon foothills near the Guinea border.
wonders.uniqueness: A community reserve protects the falls and the chimpanzees that live in the surrounding hills.

wonders.name: Lompoul Desert
wonders.summary: A small field of orange dunes near the Atlantic, between Dakar and Saint-Louis.
wonders.uniqueness: Though only about 18 km², its dunes look like the Sahara; tented camps welcome visitors.

wonders.name: Great White Pelican
wonders.summary: A huge white pelican that fishes cooperatively, herding fish in a horseshoe line.
wonders.uniqueness: Djoudj holds one of the largest breeding colonies in West Africa, with thousands of pairs. The pin is at Djoudj.

wonders.name: Baobab
wonders.summary: Senegal’s national tree: a massive trunk that stores water, with leaves, fruit and bark all put to use.
wonders.uniqueness: Baobabs can live well over 1,000 years. Their fruit pulp, bouye, is made into a drink. The baobab appears on Senegal’s coat of arms. The pin is near Thiès.

wonders.name: Gola-Tiwai Complex
wonders.summary: Sierra Leone’s largest tract of lowland rainforest, joined with Tiwai Island in the Moa River.
wonders.uniqueness: It shelters pygmy hippos, forest elephants, chimpanzees and Endangered birds such as the white-necked rockfowl. Sierra Leone’s first World Heritage Site (2025).

wonders.name: Tiwai Island
wonders.summary: A forested island in the Moa River, run as a sanctuary by local communities.
wonders.uniqueness: It has one of the highest densities of primates in the world, with 11 species including the Diana monkey.

wonders.name: Outamba-Kilimi National Park
wonders.summary: Savanna, rivers and forest in the north-west, near the Guinea border.
wonders.uniqueness: Sierra Leone’s first national park, with hippos, chimpanzees and elephants along the Little Scarcies River.

wonders.name: Mount Bintumani
wonders.summary: The highest peak in West Africa west of Mount Cameroon, at 1,945 m in the Loma Mountains.
wonders.uniqueness: Its summit grassland rises above montane forest; the source of the Niger lies just across the border in Guinea.

wonders.name: Banana Islands
wonders.summary: Three small islands off the Freetown Peninsula, with reefs and old colonial ruins.
wonders.uniqueness: Settled in the 19th century by freed Africans, the islands keep a quiet village life and clear diving waters.

media.note: No openly licensed photos of the islands yet.

wonders.name: Diana Monkey
wonders.summary: A striking black monkey with a white beard and crescent on its brow, living high in the canopy.
wonders.uniqueness: Its alarm calls distinguish leopards from eagles, and other monkeys listen in. Endangered. The pin is at Tiwai Island.

wonders.name: Freetown Cotton Tree
wonders.summary: A giant kapok tree that stood for centuries at the heart of Freetown until a storm felled it in May 2024.
wonders.uniqueness: Freed Africans who founded Freetown in 1792 are said to have prayed beneath it. Kapok trees bear pods of silky fibre once used to stuff life jackets. The pin is in Freetown.

wonders.name: Koutammakou, the Land of the Batammariba
wonders.summary: A landscape of takienta, mud tower-houses with granaries on top, in north-east Togo and north-west Benin.
wonders.uniqueness: The Batammariba build each house as a small fortress and a symbol of their cosmos. World Heritage Site since 2004, extended into Benin in 2023.

wonders.name: Fazao-Malfakassa National Park
wonders.summary: Togo’s largest national park: wooded hills, savanna and waterfalls in the centre of the country.
wonders.uniqueness: It shelters forest elephants, buffalo and many primates, in a park restored with community support.

wonders.name: Kpimé Falls
wonders.summary: A forest waterfall near Kpalimé, in the green coffee and cocoa hills of the Plateaux.
wonders.uniqueness: The hills around Kpalimé are famous for butterflies and for Mount Agou, Togo’s highest peak.

wonders.name: Lake Togo
wonders.summary: A coastal lagoon behind the sand bar east of Lomé, which gave the country its name.
wonders.uniqueness: In 1884 a treaty signed at Togoville, on its shore, began the German protectorate, and the town’s name passed to the whole country.

wonders.name: Mona Monkey
wonders.summary: A lively monkey with a white rump patch, common in the forests and mangroves of the Gulf of Guinea.
wonders.uniqueness: Mona monkeys live in groups and are protected as sacred in some villages of Togo, Ghana and Benin. The pin is near Kpalimé.

wonders.name: Red-flowered Silk-cotton Tree
wonders.summary: A savanna tree that flowers bright red on bare branches in the dry season.
wonders.uniqueness: Its flowers feed birds and are cooked in sauces; its kapok-like fibre stuffs cushions. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Mbanza Kongo
wonders.summary: The capital of the Kingdom of Kongo, one of the largest states of southern Africa from the 14th to the 19th century.
wonders.uniqueness: Renamed São Salvador after the king converted, it holds the ruins of Kulumbimbi, one of the oldest churches in sub-Saharan Africa. Angola’s first World Heritage Site (2017).

media.note: Historic views of São Salvador — no recent open photos of the site yet.

wonders.name: Kalandula Falls
wonders.summary: A horseshoe of waterfalls on the Lucala River, about 105 m high and 400 m wide.
wonders.uniqueness: One of the largest waterfalls in Africa by volume, especially in the rainy season.

wonders.name: Tundavala Gap
wonders.summary: A sheer escarpment edge near Lubango where the highlands drop more than 1,000 m towards the Namib.
wonders.uniqueness: On clear days the view runs far across the coastal plain; the gap sits at about 2,200 m.

wonders.name: Serra da Leba Pass
wonders.summary: A road of tight hairpin bends that drops down the escarpment from Lubango to Namibe.
wonders.uniqueness: Built in the 1970s, the pass is one of Angola’s best-known landmarks, a ribbon of switchbacks on a near-vertical slope.

wonders.name: Black Rocks of Pungo Andongo
wonders.summary: Giant dark rock towers rising from the savanna in Malanje.
wonders.uniqueness: Legend says footprints in the rock belong to Queen Nzinga, who resisted Portuguese conquest in the 17th century.

wonders.name: Giant Sable Antelope
wonders.summary: A black antelope with sweeping horns up to about 1.5 m, found only in central Angola. A national symbol.
wonders.uniqueness: Thought lost during the civil war, it was rediscovered by camera traps in 2005 in Cangandala. Critically Endangered. The pin is in Cangandala National Park.

media.note: Museum dioramas — the wild herds are rarely photographed.

wonders.name: Mopane
wonders.summary: A tree of hot, dry valleys with butterfly-shaped leaves that fold together in the midday heat.
wonders.uniqueness: Mopane worms, the caterpillars that feed on it, are a protein-rich delicacy across southern Africa. The pin is in southern Angola.

wonders.name: Dja Faunal Reserve
wonders.summary: One of the largest and best-protected rainforests in Africa, almost encircled by the Dja River.
wonders.uniqueness: It holds gorillas, chimpanzees, forest elephants and over 100 other mammal species. World Heritage Site since 1987.

wonders.name: Diy-Gid-Biy of the Mandara Mountains
wonders.summary: Sixteen dry-stone hilltop sites in the Mandara Mountains, built between about the 12th and 17th centuries.
wonders.uniqueness: Their builders are unknown; the name means “ruins of the chief’s house” in the Mafa language. Volcanic plugs such as Rhumsiki rise nearby. World Heritage Site since 2025.

media.note: The Mandara Mountains near Rhumsiki — no open photos of the stone sites themselves yet.

wonders.name: Mount Cameroon
wonders.summary: An active volcano rising to 4,040 m straight from the Atlantic shore, the highest peak in West and Central Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Its seaward slopes are among the wettest places on Earth. Each year runners race to the summit and back in the Race of Hope.

images.credit: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems and U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team

wonders.name: Lake Nyos
wonders.summary: A crater lake whose dissolved carbon dioxide burst out in 1986, suffocating about 1,700 people and their animals.
wonders.uniqueness: It is one of only three lakes known to have this kind of “limnic eruption”. Pipes now vent the gas from the deep water.

wonders.name: Lobé Falls
wonders.summary: A waterfall that tumbles directly into the Atlantic Ocean near Kribi.
wonders.uniqueness: Waterfalls falling straight into the sea are rare; fishermen’s pirogues paddle right up to the falls.

wonders.name: Waza National Park
wonders.summary: Sahelian savanna and floodplain near Lake Chad, with elephants, giraffes and lions.
wonders.uniqueness: Its seasonal waterholes concentrate wildlife in the dry season; it is also a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

wonders.name: Goliath Frog
wonders.summary: The largest frog on Earth, up to about 32 cm long and over 3 kg, living in fast rivers of Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea.
wonders.uniqueness: Males move stones to build nesting pools for their eggs. Endangered. The pin is in the Sanaga basin.

wonders.name: African Cherry
wonders.summary: A montane forest tree whose bark is used in medicine for prostate conditions.
wonders.uniqueness: Heavy bark-stripping for export led to its listing under CITES; Cameroon’s highlands are a major source. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Manovo-Gounda St Floris National Park
wonders.summary: Wide floodplain savanna in the north, once one of Africa’s richest wildlife areas.
wonders.uniqueness: Poaching devastated its rhinos and elephants; it has been on the List in Danger since 1997. World Heritage Site since 1988.

wonders.name: Dzanga Bai
wonders.summary: A mineral-rich forest clearing where up to about 100 forest elephants gather at once.
wonders.uniqueness: Researchers have recorded thousands of individual elephants here since 1990. It lies in Dzanga-Sangha, part of the Sangha Trinational World Heritage Site.

wonders.name: Boali Falls
wonders.summary: A curtain of water about 50 m high on the Mbali River, north-west of Bangui.
wonders.uniqueness: A hydroelectric plant here supplies much of Bangui’s power; in the rainy season the falls spread wide.

wonders.name: Ubangi River
wonders.summary: The great river that forms the border with DR Congo, flowing past Bangui to join the Congo.
wonders.uniqueness: It is the largest right-bank tributary of the Congo and the country’s main route to the sea.

wonders.name: African Forest Elephant
wonders.summary: A smaller elephant of the rainforest with straight, downward-pointing tusks.
wonders.uniqueness: Recognised as a separate species, it spreads the seeds of many trees. Critically Endangered after heavy ivory poaching. The pin is at Dzanga Bai.

wonders.name: Koko
wonders.summary: A forest vine whose leaves are sliced thin and cooked as a favourite green across Central Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Gathered wild and traded across borders, it is a key source of income for forest families. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Lakes of Ounianga
wonders.summary: Eighteen lakes in the Sahara, fed by fossil groundwater, in one of the driest places on Earth.
wonders.uniqueness: Some are fresh, others salty and red with algae; floating reeds slow evaporation. World Heritage Site since 2012.

wonders.name: Ennedi Massif
wonders.summary: A sandstone plateau of arches, pillars and canyons in north-east Chad.
wonders.uniqueness: Gueltas such as Guelta d’Archei shelter some of the last Saharan crocodiles, and the rock shelters hold thousands of paintings. Mixed World Heritage Site since 2016.

wonders.name: Zakouma National Park
wonders.summary: Floodplain savanna in south-east Chad where elephant numbers are rising again after a poaching crisis.
wonders.uniqueness: Managed with African Parks since 2010, it has seen elephant herds grow and lions and black rhinos return.

wonders.name: Lake Chad
wonders.summary: A shallow lake shared by Chad, Cameroon, Niger and Nigeria, famous for its dramatic changes in size.
wonders.uniqueness: It shrank from about 25,000 km² in the 1960s to a fraction of that, and swells and shrinks with the rains, supporting millions of people.

wonders.name: Emi Koussi
wonders.summary: The highest peak of the Sahara at 3,415 m, a huge shield volcano in the Tibesti Mountains.
wonders.uniqueness: Its summit caldera is about 15 km wide, and the Tibesti’s volcanoes are among the least visited on Earth.

wonders.name: Kordofan Giraffe
wonders.summary: A giraffe of the central African savannas, with pale patches and spotted legs.
wonders.uniqueness: Zakouma holds one of its largest remaining populations. Critically Endangered. The pin is in Zakouma.

media.note: Zoo animals — Kordofan giraffes in the wild live in Zakouma and Garamba.

wonders.name: Desert Date
wonders.summary: A spiny Sahel tree whose sweet-bitter fruit, oil and leaves are used in food and medicine.
wonders.uniqueness: It thrives where few other trees can, and is one of the species planted for Africa’s Great Green Wall. The pin is a representative point.

wonders.name: Virunga National Park
wonders.summary: Africa’s oldest national park (1925), from lava plains and active volcanoes to the glaciers of the Rwenzori.
wonders.uniqueness: It shelters about a third of the world’s mountain gorillas, along with hippos on Lake Edward. On the List in Danger since 1994.

wonders.name: Garamba National Park
wonders.summary: Savanna and gallery forest on the South Sudan border, one of Africa’s oldest parks.
wonders.uniqueness: It was the last stronghold of the northern white rhino in the wild. It still holds Kordofan giraffes and elephants. World Heritage Site since 1980.

images.credit: Matthew Luizza / U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service

wonders.name: Kahuzi-Biega National Park
wonders.summary: Montane and lowland forest west of Lake Kivu, dominated by the extinct volcanoes Kahuzi and Biega.
wonders.uniqueness: It protects the eastern lowland (Grauer’s) gorilla, the largest gorilla subspecies. On the List in Danger since 1997.

wonders.name: Salonga National Park
wonders.summary: Africa’s largest tropical rainforest reserve, reachable only by river.
wonders.uniqueness: It covers about 36,000 km² and is home to the bonobo, forest elephant and Congo peafowl. Removed from the List in Danger in 2021.

media.note: No openly licensed photos of Salonga yet.

wonders.name: Okapi Wildlife Reserve
wonders.summary: The Ituri Forest, home of the okapi and of Mbuti hunter-gatherers.
wonders.uniqueness: It holds an estimated 5,000 okapi, a large share of those left in the wild. On the List in Danger since 1997.

wonders.name: Nyiragongo
wonders.summary: An active volcano above Goma, with one of the largest lava lakes on Earth in its crater.
wonders.uniqueness: Its lava is unusually fluid; eruptions in 1977, 2002 and 2021 sent flows towards the city.

wonders.name: Boyoma Falls
wonders.summary: Seven cataracts on the upper Congo near Kisangani, over about 100 km of river.
wonders.uniqueness: By the volume of water, they are often cited as the largest waterfalls in the world. Wagenya fishermen fish them with wooden tripods and basket traps.

wonders.name: Livingstone Falls
wonders.summary: A chain of huge rapids where the Congo drops about 270 m on its way from Kinshasa to the sea.
wonders.uniqueness: The rapids stopped navigation upstream, so early travellers had to go overland. Some stretches are among the deepest river channels known.

wonders.name: Bonobo
wonders.summary: The great ape found only south of the Congo River, our closest living relative along with the chimpanzee.
wonders.uniqueness: Bonobo societies are led by females and settle tension through social bonds rather than fighting. Endangered. The pin is in the Salonga area.

wonders.name: Limbali
wonders.summary: A canopy tree that forms almost single-species forests along the rivers of the Congo basin.
wonders.uniqueness: Limbali stands cast deep shade and drop large seeds that sprout under their parents, letting one species dominate a whole forest. The pin is in the Ituri.

wonders.name: Sangha Trinational
wonders.summary: Some 7,500 km² of rainforest joining parks in Congo, Cameroon and the Central African Republic.
wonders.uniqueness: Its clearings attract forest elephants, gorillas and bongos. Researchers here filmed wild gorillas using sticks as tools. World Heritage Site since 2012.

wonders.name: Forest Massif of Odzala-Kokoua
wonders.summary: Rainforest and savanna clearings in north-west Congo with one of Africa’s densest gorilla populations.
wonders.uniqueness: Protected since 1935, one of Africa’s oldest parks, it holds western lowland gorillas, chimpanzees and forest elephants. World Heritage Site since 2023.

wonders.name: Congo Rapids at Brazzaville
wonders.summary: The Congo River leaves Malebo Pool in thundering rapids between Brazzaville and Kinshasa.
wonders.uniqueness: The two capitals face each other across the river, the closest pair of capitals in the world apart from Rome and Vatican City.

wonders.name: Conkouati-Douli National Park
wonders.summary: A coastal park of lagoons, savanna and forest where turtles nest and chimpanzees are released.
wonders.uniqueness: It is one of the most diverse protected areas in Congo, from the ocean to the Mayombe mountains.

wonders.name: Western Lowland Gorilla
wonders.summary: The most numerous gorilla, living in the swamp and lowland forests of the Congo basin.
wonders.uniqueness: Most of the world’s western lowland gorillas live in Congo and Gabon, but Ebola and poaching have cut numbers sharply. Critically Endangered. The pin is in Odzala.

wonders.name: African Tulip Tree
wonders.summary: A forest tree with fiery orange cup-shaped flowers, native to tropical Central and West Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Planted in gardens across the tropics, it is invasive in some islands. Its flower cups hold rain and nectar for birds. The pin is near Brazzaville.

wonders.name: Pico Basilé
wonders.summary: The highest point of Equatorial Guinea at 3,011 m, a volcano rising over Malabo on Bioko.
wonders.uniqueness: Cloud forest on its slopes is home to endemic birds and primates found only on Bioko.

wonders.name: Monte Alén National Park
wonders.summary: The largest park in mainland Equatorial Guinea, a rainforest of rivers and granite peaks.
wonders.uniqueness: It holds gorillas, chimpanzees, forest elephants and many butterflies, across about 2,000 km².

wonders.name: Ureca Beaches
wonders.summary: Black-sand beaches on the remote south coast of Bioko.
wonders.uniqueness: Four species of sea turtle nest here, including leatherbacks and green turtles, monitored by local and university teams.

wonders.name: Bioko Drill
wonders.summary: A short-tailed forest monkey related to the mandrill, with a black face and red lower lip.
wonders.uniqueness: The drill is one of Africa’s most endangered primates; the Bioko form lives only on the island, threatened by bushmeat hunting. The pin is in southern Bioko.

wonders.name: God Tree
wonders.summary: A giant silk-cotton tree, the emblem on Equatorial Guinea’s coat of arms.
wonders.uniqueness: Tradition holds that an early treaty between Spain and a local ruler was signed beneath such a tree. Kapok trees can top 60 m. The pin is near Malabo.

wonders.name: Lopé-Okanda
wonders.summary: Rainforest and relict savannas along the Ogooué, with traces of people stretching back 400,000 years.
wonders.uniqueness: Around 1,800 rock engravings and Iron Age sites lie among mandrill troops of up to several hundred. Mixed World Heritage Site since 2007.

wonders.name: Ivindo National Park
wonders.summary: Blackwater rivers and waterfalls such as Kongou in the heart of Gabon’s forest.
wonders.uniqueness: The Langoué Bai clearing draws forest elephants and gorillas. World Heritage Site since 2021.

wonders.name: Loango National Park
wonders.summary: Lagoons, forest and beaches where elephants, buffalo and hippos walk on the sand.
wonders.uniqueness: Called “Africa’s last Eden”; hippos have been filmed swimming in the surf, and humpback whales pass offshore.

wonders.name: Pongara National Park
wonders.summary: Mangroves and beaches across the estuary from Libreville.
wonders.uniqueness: Its beaches are among the most important leatherback turtle nesting sites in the world.

wonders.name: Monts de Cristal
wonders.summary: Misty low mountains near the Equatorial Guinea border, among the richest plant areas in Africa.
wonders.uniqueness: Botanists have recorded many endemic begonias and orchids here.

wonders.name: Mandrill
wonders.summary: The most colourful primate, with a red and blue face, living in large forest troops.
wonders.uniqueness: Lopé hosts “hordes” of more than 800 mandrills, the largest groups of any primate apart from humans. The pin is in Lopé.

wonders.name: Okoumé
wonders.summary: Gabon’s signature timber tree, a tall softwood of the coastal forest.
wonders.uniqueness: For a century it was the backbone of Gabon’s economy, shipped for plywood; since 2010 Gabon has required logs to be processed in the country. The pin is a representative point.

media.note: An okoumé being felled in French Equatorial Africa, early 20th century.

wonders.name: The Roças of São Tomé and Príncipe
wonders.summary: Plantation estates that made the islands among the world’s top cocoa producers in the early 1900s, built on forced labour.
wonders.uniqueness: Hospitals, workers’ quarters and drying sheds survive at roças such as Agostinho Neto. Inscribed in 2026 as a record of colonial agriculture and forced migration.

wonders.name: Pico Cão Grande
wonders.summary: A needle of volcanic rock rising about 370 m above the forest of southern São Tomé.
wonders.uniqueness: It is a volcanic plug, the hardened core of an old volcano; its sheer sides were first climbed in 1991.

wonders.name: Obô Natural Park
wonders.summary: Cloud forest and lowland rainforest covering much of the interior of both islands.
wonders.uniqueness: The islands have exceptional numbers of endemic birds, frogs and plants for their size, many protected here.

wonders.name: Boca do Inferno
wonders.summary: A blowhole on the east coast where Atlantic waves surge through a lava tunnel.
wonders.uniqueness: Spray bursts high from the black volcanic rock at high tide.

wonders.name: Giant Sunbird
wonders.summary: The largest sunbird in the world, found only in the forests of São Tomé.
wonders.uniqueness: At about 23 cm it is twice the length of most sunbirds. Vulnerable. The pin is in Obô Natural Park.

wonders.name: Giant Begonia
wonders.summary: A begonia that grows taller than a person, found only on São Tomé.
wonders.uniqueness: Its stems can reach about 2–3 m, among the largest of any begonia. The pin is in the cloud forest.
